Weaker than -1 and the gate doesn't close enough, so it gets pulled to the lure and pricked; too strong like -3 and the gate closes even in front of real food, so it stops. 실제 뉴런 중에는 자극이 없어도 스스로 발화하는 것들이 있다(자발 발화): Some real neurons fire on their own with no stimulus at all (spontaneous firing). The spinal cord even has circuits that make a walking rhythm without commands from the brain (central pattern generators).
인공신경망의 모든 뉴런에는 편향(b)이 있다. y = w·x + b에서: Every neuron in an artificial neural network has a bias (b). In y = w·x + b, b is "the base value that comes out even when the input is 0," and it moves the decision boundary away from the origin. The weight coming from the always-on neuron is exactly the bias. Grillner (2006) calls circuits that make rhythm without commands from the brain "central pattern generators."
The left senses move the right side of the body.
사람의 왼쪽 대뇌는 몸의 오른쪽을, 오른쪽 대뇌는 왼쪽을 맡는다(대측 지: In people, the left cerebrum controls the right side of the body and the right cerebrum the left (contralateral control). This is because most bundles of motor nerves cross over left and right in the medulla on the way down.
발렌티노 브라이텐베르크는 책 『Vehicles』(1984)에서 센서 두: In his book "Vehicles" (1984), Valentino Braitenberg showed that vehicles with just two sensors and two wheels can show behaviors like "aggression," "fear," and "love." Crossed excitation makes an "aggression" vehicle that rushes at the light. That's the brain you just built. The first robot of this kind that sought light was Walter's (1950) robot tortoise ("An imitation of life").
The body dodges before you think.
뜨거운 냄비에 손이 닿으면 대뇌가 \"뜨겁다\"를 알아채기 전에 척수가: When your hand touches a hot pan, the spinal cord sends a signal to the arm muscles before the cerebrum even notices "hot!" This short path from sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron is called a reflex arc.
입력을 출력에 바로 잇는 것은 \"규칙 기반\" 제어와 같다. 로봇 청소: Connecting inputs straight to outputs is like "rule-based" control. Like a robot vacuum that turns the moment its bumper sensor touches something, the computation is short, so it's fast and reliable. But when situations get complicated, the rules clash. Castellucci, Kandel and colleagues (1970) showed, at the level of a few neurons, how the sea slug's "gill-withdrawal reflex" weakens with repetition ("habituation").
Subtracting signals matters as much as adding them.
뇌의 뉴런 중 상당수는 다른 뉴런을 조용하게 만드는 억제성 뉴런이다. 대: Many neurons in the brain are inhibitory neurons that quiet other neurons. The best-known inhibitory transmitter is GABA. When the balance between excitation and inhibition breaks down, signals can spread out of control; epileptic seizures are a well-known example.
인공신경망에서 억제는 음수 가중치다. 이 실험의 생명체는 빛이 셀수록 바: In artificial neural networks, inhibition is a negative weight. The creature in this experiment slows down as the light gets stronger and stops in front of it. Braitenberg called this "love." With the same two neurons, a single sign flips the personality completely. Hartline and colleagues (1956) directly measured "inhibition" between neighboring visual cells in the horseshoe crab's eye.
One spot in the brain for each whisker.
쥐는 수염을 앞뒤로 흔들며 주변을 더듬는다. 쥐 대뇌 겉질의 체성감각 영: Rats sweep their whiskers back and forth to feel their surroundings. In the somatosensory area of the rat cortex, clumps of neurons called "barrels," one for each whisker, are lined up exactly like the whiskers themselves.
여러 감각을 한 뇌에서 합치는 것을 감각 통합(멀티모달)이라고 한다. 지: Combining several senses in one brain is called sensory integration (multimodal). Right now the creature's wheels receive a weighted sum of eye and whisker signals. Different senses compete for the same output, and the weights decide who wins. Woolsey and Van der Loos (1970) found these clumps of neurons in the mouse cortex and named them "barrels" after their shape.
A middle neuron, invisible from outside, that takes from inputs and passes only to other neurons.
감각 뉴런과 운동 뉴런 사이를 잇는 뉴런을 개재뉴런(사이뉴런)이라고 한다: Neurons that connect sensory neurons and motor neurons are called interneurons. Even in the roundworm, which has only 302 neurons, a large share are interneurons. "Decisions" such as whether to avoid or approach happen here.
은닉층이다. 이 게임의 히든 뉴런은 0 아래로 내려가지 않고 1에서 잘리: This is the hidden layer. Hidden neurons in this game use a nonlinear function that never goes below 0 and is cut off at 1 (clip to 0–1). ReLU, widely used today, is also a nonlinear function that cuts off below 0. Because the function bends like this, it can make judgments a single straight line can't, such as "a gate that blocks the light signal only when there's danger." It's the same reason a multilayer perceptron solved XOR when a single perceptron couldn't. Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams (1986) called these neurons "hidden units."
A fake more real than the real thing.
실제 아귀는 머리에서 뻗은 낚싯대 끝의 빛나는 미끼(에스카)로 먹이를 꾀: A real anglerfish lures prey with a glowing bait (the esca) at the tip of a fishing rod growing from its head. The bait's glow is made by luminous bacteria living inside it. It turns the prey's brain rule "light = food" against it.
사람 눈에는 똑같아 보이는데 인공지능은 완전히 틀리게 판단하는 입력을 적: An input that looks the same to a person but makes an AI judge completely wrong is called an adversarial example. A famous experiment added tiny noise to a photo of a panda and the AI classified it as a gibbon. The simpler the rule, the weaker it is against lures like this. The name "adversarial examples" was given by Szegedy and colleagues (2013), and the panda → gibbon example appears in Goodfellow and colleagues (2014).
A map of every connection in a brain.
커넥톰은 뇌의 뉴런과 시냅스를 빠짐없이 그린 배선도다. 꼬마선충(뉴런 3: A connectome is a wiring diagram that draws every neuron and synapse of a brain. The roundworm (302 neurons) was completed first, and in 2024 the FlyWire team published the whole brain of an adult fruit fly (about 140,000 neurons and about 50 million synapses). The human brain has about 86 billion neurons.
The brains you build in this game are small connectomes. Know the wiring and the behavior is decided. But is that really so? Real connectome research faces the question that, even with the same wiring, behavior changes with synapse strength, neuromodulators, and the body and environment. The word "connectome" appeared in 2005, but the roundworm nervous system wiring diagram drawn by White and colleagues (1986) was the first connectome.
뉴런은 들어온 신호에 \"가중치\"를 곱해서 받는다. 출력이 입력 A를: A neuron receives incoming signals multiplied by a "weight." Make the output copy input A exactly. The output reads as 1 if it's 0.5 or more and 0 if below.
시냅스 하나는 \"보내는 뉴런의 값 × 가중치\"를 받는 뉴런에게 더해: One synapse adds "sending neuron's value × weight" to the receiving neuron.
값 조절: 가중치가 0.5보다 작으면 A가 1이어도 출력이 0.5를 못: Tuning: if the weight is below 0.5, the output can't reach 0.5 even when A is 1. 0.5 or more works. Even if you raise the weight to 3, the output is cut off at 1.
여러 시냅스가 한 뉴런으로 들어오면 신호가 모두 더해진다(가중합). A나: When several synapses come into one neuron, all the signals are added up (weighted sum). Make the output turn on if either A or B is on. As a logic gate, this is OR.
The values coming into the output neuron are all added up and then clipped to 0–1.
Tuning: if the weights of A and B are both 0.5 or more, either one alone is enough to pass 0.5. If either is below 0.5, it fails when only that one is on.
Input A → output +1, input B → output +1.
A와 B가 모두 켜졌을 때만 출력이 켜지게 해 보자(AND). 하나만 켜: Make the output turn on only when both A and B are on (AND). You need to raise the "threshold" so that one alone can't get over it.
상시 뉴런은 언제나 1이다. 상시 → 출력을 음수로 이으면 출력이 넘어야: The always-on neuron is always 1. Connect always-on → output with a negative value, and the threshold the output has to get over rises. This is the bias.
값 조절: A, B가 +1이면 상시는 -1 근처(-0.6 ~ -1.4)가: Tuning: with A and B at +1, always-on works around -1 (-0.6 to -1.4). Close to 0 and one alone gets over it; stronger than -1.5 and even both together can't. Or you can skip the bias and make A and B small, 0.25–0.49.
Input A → output +1, input B → output +1, always-on → output -1.
A가 꺼져 있을 때 켜지고, A가 켜지면 꺼지는 출력을 만들어 보자(NO: Make an output that's on when A is off and off when A is on (NOT). Time to use a negative weight.
아무것도 안 켜졌을 때도 출력이 켜져야 한다. 그러려면 언제나 1인 상시: The output must be on even when nothing is on. For that you need the always-on neuron, which is always 1.
값 조절: 상시 → 출력은 0.5 이상(+1이면 충분). A → 출력은: Tuning: always-on → output 0.5 or more (+1 is enough). A → output negative, at least 0.5 smaller than the always-on value (-0.6 or less if always-on is +1).
A와 B 중 딱 하나만 켜졌을 때 출력이 켜지게 해 보자(XOR). 출력: Make the output turn on when exactly one of A and B is on (XOR). No weights can do this with a single output neuron. You need two hidden neurons.
히든 뉴런은 0 아래로 내려가지 않는다. \"A는 켜지고 B는 꺼졌을 때: Hidden neurons never go below 0. Put a neuron that's "1 only when A is on and B is off" in hidden 1, the opposite in hidden 2, and add them at the output.
값 조절: 히든 1 = A × (+1) + B × (-1). A·B가 둘: Tuning: hidden 1 = A × (+1) + B × (-1). When A and B are both on it must become 0, so the negative side must be as big as the positive side (+1 / -1). Hidden neuron → output at +1 is enough.
A → 히든 1 +1, B → 히든 1 -1, B → 히든 2 +1, A: A → hidden 1 +1, B → hidden 1 -1, B → hidden 2 +1, A → hidden 2 -1, hidden 1 → output +1, hidden 2 → output +1.
이번에는 가중치를 직접 고치지 않는다. 뉴런이 틀린 만큼 스스로 가중치를: This time you don't fix the weights yourself. The neuron fixes its own weights by as much as it was wrong. Press "Learn once" and watch it learn OR. All weights start at 0.

Watch the error graph. With a good learning rate, the error goes down steadily.

뉴런 하나에게 XOR을 가르쳐 보자. 학습률을 바꿔 가며 50번 이상 학: Try teaching XOR to a single neuron. Change the learning rate, train 50 rounds or more, and watch what happens to the error. You clear this experiment by confirming that it "fails."
‘하나만 켜져야’(XOR) 실험을 떠올려 보자. 그때도 출력 뉴런 하나로: Remember the "Exactly One" (XOR) experiment. Back then, one output neuron couldn't do it either.
값 조절: 학습률을 아무리 바꿔도 오차가 0으로 가지 않는다. 작은 학습: Tuning: however you change the learning rate, the error doesn't go to 0. With a small learning rate the error stalls around 0.25; with a big one it actually grows.
Run Auto-learn at learning rates 0.1 and 1 to fill 50 rounds.
히든 뉴런 두 개를 넣었다. 이제 출력의 오차를 히든 뉴런에게도 거꾸로: Two hidden neurons have been added. Now the output's error is passed backward to the hidden neurons too, and every weight gets fixed. Can it learn the XOR that one neuron couldn't?
히든 뉴런이 출력에 크게 이어져 있을수록 오차를 많이 나눠 받는다. 히든: The more strongly a hidden neuron connects to the output, the more of the error it receives. If a hidden neuron's value is stuck at 0 or 1, that neuron doesn't learn.
값 조절: 0.02면 10번, 0.1이면 3번, 0.5면 2번 만에 배운: Tuning: at 0.02 it learns in 10 rounds, at 0.1 in 3, at 0.5 in 2. At 1 or more the hidden neurons get stuck at 0 or 1 and can't learn any more.
A가 켜졌고, B는 꺼졌을 때만 출력이 켜지게 하자. \"그리고\"와 \: Make the output turn on only when A is on and B is off. You have to fit both "and" and "not" into one neuron.
켜지게 하는 신호와 끄는 신호를 따로 생각해 보자. 무엇이 출력을 켜고,: Think separately about the signal that turns it on and the signal that turns it off. What should turn the output on, and what should block it?
Tuning: A positive, B negative. For the sum to drop below 0.5 when both A and B are on, B must be at least as strong as A.
Input A → output +1, input B → output -1.
A와 B가 같을 때(둘 다 꺼졌거나 둘 다 켜졌을 때) 출력이 켜지게 하: Make the output turn on when A and B are the same (both off or both on). Split it into two cases and give each to a hidden neuron.
\"같다\" = \"둘 다 켜짐\" 또는 \"둘 다 꺼짐\". 두 경우를: "Equal" = "both on" or "both off." Make one neuron for each case and combine them with OR at the output.
값 조절: \"둘 다 켜짐\"은 A +1, B +1, 상시 -1. \"둘: Tuning: "both on" is A +1, B +1, always-on -1. "Both off" is always-on +1, A -1, B -1. The output just adds the two hidden neurons at +1.
히든 1 = A +1, B +1, 상시 -1 / 히든 2 = 상시 +1,: Hidden 1 = A +1, B +1, always-on -1 / hidden 2 = always-on +1, A -1, B -1 / hidden 1 and 2 → output +1.
세 명이 투표한다. A, B, C 중 두 명 이상이 켜지면(찬성하면) 출: Three people vote. Make the output turn on when two or more of A, B, C are on (vote yes).
세 입력을 똑같은 세기로 더하면 \"몇 명이 켰는지\"가 된다. 문제는: Add the three inputs with the same strength and you get "how many are on." The problem is the threshold that separates 1 person from 2.
Tuning: with A, B, C all at +1, one person = 1 and two = 2. Set always-on to -1 and one person = 0 (off), two = 1 (on). If always-on is -0.5, even one person gives 0.5 and it turns on.
A, B, C → output +1, always-on → output -1.
A, B, C 중 정확히 한 명만 켰을 때 출력이 켜지게 하자. 한 번에: Make the output turn on when exactly one of A, B, C is on. If it's hard to solve in one go, split the problem.
"Exactly one" = "one or more" and "not two or more." Give the two conditions to two hidden neurons, one each.
값 조절: 히든 1 = A+B+C(하나 이상이면 1). 히든 2 = A+: Tuning: hidden 1 = A+B+C (1 if one or more). Hidden 2 = A+B+C-1 (1 if two or more). Output = hidden 1 +1, hidden 2 -1. Because hidden neurons are cut off at 1, even with all three on it becomes 1 - 1 = 0.
A·B·C → 히든 1 +1 / A·B·C → 히든 2 +1, 상시 →: A, B, C → hidden 1 +1 / A, B, C → hidden 2 +1, always-on → hidden 2 -1 / hidden 1 → output +1, hidden 2 → output -1.
A와 B를 더하는 회로를 만들자. 1 + 1 = 10(이진수)이다. 출력: Build a circuit that adds A and B. 1 + 1 = 10 (in binary). Output is the sum for this digit, and output 2 is the carry to the next digit.
두 출력을 따로따로 생각하자. 합은 \"하나만 켜짐\", 올림은 \"둘: Think about the two outputs separately. The sum is "only one on," and the carry is "both on." Remember the XOR and AND from the "One Neuron" chapter.
값 조절: 올림(출력 2)은 A +1, B +1, 상시 -1. 합(출력): Tuning: carry (output 2) is A +1, B +1, always-on -1. For the sum (output), make hidden 1 = A - B and hidden 2 = B - A and add them. Hidden neurons never go below 0, so when A = B both become 0.
A → 히든 1 +1, B → 히든 1 -1, B → 히든 2 +1, A: A → hidden 1 +1, B → hidden 1 -1, B → hidden 2 +1, A → hidden 2 -1, hidden 1 and 2 → output +1 / A, B → output 2 +1, always-on → output 2 -1.
A와 B가 둘 다 켜졌을 때만 꺼지는 출력(NAND)을 만들자. 단, 별: Make an output that turns off only when both A and B are on (NAND). But to get all the stars, you may only use +1 and -1 as weights. Without values like 0.5, how do you make a threshold?
NAND = NOT(AND). AND를 먼저 히든 뉴런에서 만들고, 출력: NAND = NOT(AND). Build AND in a hidden neuron first, then flip it at the output.
값 조절: 히든 1 = A +1, B +1, 상시 -1이면 AND다. 출: Tuning: hidden 1 = A +1, B +1, always-on -1 is AND. Output = always-on +1, hidden 1 -1 becomes 0 only when AND is on. Everything uses only +1 and -1.
A·B → 히든 1 +1, 상시 → 히든 1 -1 / 상시 → 출력 +1: A, B → hidden 1 +1, always-on → hidden 1 -1 / always-on → output +1, hidden 1 → output -1.
A signal that turns on and a signal that blocks, together.
뇌에서는 흥분 신호와 억제 신호가 한 뉴런에 함께 들어온다. 억제가 이기: In the brain, excitatory and inhibitory signals come into the same neuron together. If inhibition wins, the neuron doesn't fire even when excitation arrives. That's how conditions like "this, but not that" are made.
논리로는 A AND (NOT B)다. \"로그인했고, 차단당하지 않았으면: In logic it's A AND (NOT B). Most conditions in programs look like this, as in "you can enter if you're logged in and not banned." Shannon (1938) showed that logic formulas like this can be carried straight over into "relay and switching circuits."
어려운 판단을 여러 뉴런이 나눠 맡고, 다음 뉴런이 그 결과를 모으는 방: Brain circuits often split a hard judgment among several neurons and let the next neuron gather the results.
"Equal" (XNOR) is "both 1" OR "both 0." Splitting a big condition into small cases and combining them at the end is the most common way of thinking in coding and math. Shannon (1938) showed how to turn logic formulas that split and combine cases into circuits with switches in series and parallel ("symbolic analysis").
Count, then compare with the threshold.
뉴런은 여러 입력을 더해 문턱과 비교한다. 많은 입력이 동시에 들어와야: A neuron adds up its inputs and compares the total with a threshold. Firing only when many inputs arrive at once is one of the ways the brain filters out noise.
여러 모델의 답을 모아 투표로 정하는 것을 앙상블이라고 한다. 모델 하나: Gathering the answers of several models and deciding by vote is called an ensemble. Even if one model is wrong, the right answer comes out if most are right. McCulloch and Pitts's (1943) neuron is also a majority element that turns on when the number of active inputs passes a "threshold."
"Exactly one" = "one or more" and "not two or more."
뇌는 복잡한 판단을 단계로 나눠 처리한다. 앞 단계 뉴런이 단순한 조건을: The brain handles complex judgments in stages. Earlier-stage neurons judge simple conditions, and later-stage neurons combine them.
한 번에 풀기 어려운 문제를 풀 수 있는 작은 문제로 나누는 것을 분할: Splitting a problem that's hard to solve at once into small solvable problems is called divide and conquer. The hidden layer of a neural network builds in-between conditions the same way. Shannon (1938) set out how to break complex conditions into small logic formulas and assemble them into switching circuits ("symbolic analysis").
사람의 뇌는 이진수로 더하지 않는다. 대신 수를 대략적인 크기로 느끼는: The human brain doesn't add in binary. Instead, it's known to have a separate area (the parietal lobe) that senses numbers by rough size.
컴퓨터의 덧셈은 XOR(그 자리의 합)과 AND(올림)로 만든 반가산기에: A computer's addition starts from the half adder, built from XOR (the sum for this digit) and AND (the carry). Chain half adders together and you can add numbers with any number of digits. In this paper, Shannon (1938) actually designed a binary adder from switching circuits ("electric adder to the base two").
뇌의 뉴런도 종류는 많지 않지만, 연결 방식에 따라 전혀 다른 일을 한다: The brain has only a few kinds of neurons too, but depending on how they connect, they do completely different jobs. The wiring matters more than the parts.
NAND 게이트만 있으면 AND, OR, NOT은 물론 어떤 논리 회로든: With only NAND gates you can build AND, OR, NOT and indeed any logic circuit (a universal gate). Real computer chips are also made of billions of simple gates like NAND. Sheffer (1913) showed that all of Boolean algebra can be built from a single operation, "neither ... nor" (NOR). NAND, which has the same property, was first used by Nicod in 1917, and today both are called the "Sheffer stroke."
이번에는 뇌를 직접 잇지 않는다. 생명체가 할 수 있는 일마다 점수를 정: This time you don't wire the brain directly. Give points for each thing the creature can do, and the creature finds a brain that earns many points by trial and error. To make it eat 3 pieces of food, what should you give points for?
생명체는 \"점수의 합\"이 커지는 쪽으로만 바뀐다. 우리가 원하는 일(: The creature only changes in the direction that makes the "sum of points" bigger. You have to give points for the thing you want (eating food) for it to learn that.
값 조절: \"시간이 지나면\"에만 점수를 주면 가만히 있어도 점수가 똑: Tuning: if you only give points for "As time passes," points pile up equally even if it stays still, so it learns nothing. With exploration at 0.1 it changes too little and can't find the first food.
Start learning with "When it eats food" +5 and exploration 0.3.
This time all the food is behind the creature, and there are only 12 generations to learn. If you give points only for eating, it can't tell which way is good until it happens to eat. Try giving points for getting closer to food too.
12세대 안에 먹이 3개를 먹게 하기: Make it eat 3 pieces of food within 12 generations
보상이 너무 드물면(희소 보상) 배울 실마리가 없다. 목표로 가는 중간: If rewards are too rare (sparse rewards), there's no clue to learn from. Give small points for the steps along the way to the goal and the path becomes easier to find.
값 조절: \"먹이를 먹으면\"만 주면 26세대쯤 걸려서 12세대 안에는: Tuning: with only "When it eats food" it takes about 26 generations, so it can't learn within 12. Add "When it gets closer to food" +1 and it learns in about 7 generations (exploration 0.3). Exploration 0.6 is even faster.
\"먹이를 먹으면\" +5, \"먹이에 가까워지면\" +1, 탐험 정도: "When it eats food" +5, "When it gets closer to food" +1, exploration 0.3.
먹이 가는 길에 가시가 있다. 이 실험에서는 가시에 찔려도 시간 손해가: There are thorns on the way to the food. In this experiment, getting pricked costs no time. Then the creature has no reason to care about thorns. How do you make it eat without getting pricked even once?
가시에 한 번도 찔리지 않고 먹이 3개: 3 pieces of food without a single thorn prick
보상은 음수가 될 수도 있다. 피하게 하고 싶은 일에는 벌점을 줘야 한다: Rewards can be negative too. Give a penalty for things you want it to avoid. The creature has feelers, so it can sense the thorns.
값 조절: 벌점이 없으면 가시를 그냥 뚫고 지나가는 게 가장 빠른 길이라: Tuning: without a penalty, going straight through the thorns is the fastest way, so it gets pricked. Give "When pricked by a thorn" -5 and it learns to go around. Weak like -1 and it takes longer to learn (about 16 generations; at -5 about 12).
\"먹이를 먹으면\" +5, \"먹이에 가까워지면\" +1, \"가시에: "When it eats food" +5, "When it gets closer to food" +1, "When pricked by a thorn" -5, exploration 0.3.
누군가 \"많이 돌아다니면 먹이도 많이 찾겠지\"라고 생각해서 점수 규칙: Someone thought "if it moves around a lot, it'll find lots of food" and set the reward rules in advance (moving +3, eating food +1). Train it as is and watch what it learns, then fix the rules so it reaches the real goal.
생명체는 우리가 원한 것이 아니라 점수를 준 것을 배운다. 먼저 정해진: The creature learns what you gave points for, not what you wanted. First train it with the rules as they are. The points go up, but it hardly eats any food.
값 조절: \"움직이면\" +3이 문제다. 빨리 빙빙 도는 것만으로 먹이: Tuning: "When it moves" +3 is the problem. Just spinning around fast earns far more points than food. Lower "When it moves" to 0, and give points for eating food and for getting closer to food.
\"움직이면\" 0, \"먹이를 먹으면\" +5, \"먹이에 가까워지면\: "When it moves" 0, "When it eats food" +5, "When it gets closer to food" +1, exploration 0.3.
이번에는 진리표 대신 평면 위의 점들이다. 뉴런은 점의 x·y 좌표를 받: This time, instead of a truth table, there are points on a plane. The neuron takes a point's x and y coordinates and answers blue if the output is 0.5 or more, orange if below. The background color is the brain's answer everywhere on the plane, and the line where the two colors meet is the "decision boundary." Separate the blue on the right from the orange on the left.
x 좌표가 클수록 파랑이다. x 좌표 → 출력을 이으면 오른쪽일수록 출력: The bigger the x coordinate, the bluer. Connect x coordinate → output and the output grows toward the right.
값 조절: x → 출력 가중치를 키우면 경계가 가팔라지고, 상시(편향)를: Tuning: raise the x → output weight and the boundary gets steeper; make always-on (bias) negative and the boundary is pushed right. The boundary is where "x × weight + bias = 0.5." With weight 2 and bias -0.5, the boundary stands at x = 0.5.
이번에는 경계가 비스듬하다. 오른쪽 위는 파랑, 왼쪽 아래는 주황. x와: This time the boundary is slanted. Top right is blue, bottom left is orange. You have to use x and y together. The weights set the line's slope, and the bias sets its position.
The bigger both x and y, the bluer. Connect both to the output.
값 조절: x와 y의 가중치가 같으면 경계는 45° 대각선이 된다. 둘: Tuning: if x and y have the same weight, the boundary is a 45° diagonal. With both at +1, to split near x + y = 1 the bias must be -0.5 (1 - 0.5 = 0.5). Raise only one weight and the line tilts that way.
x 좌표 → 출력 +1, y 좌표 → 출력 +1, 상시 → 출력 -0.5: x coordinate → output +1, y coordinate → output +1, always-on → output -0.5.
파랑이 가운데 세로 띠에만 있고, 주황은 양쪽에 있다. 직선 하나로는 띠: Blue is only in a vertical band in the middle, with orange on both sides. One straight line can't make a band. Use two hidden neurons to make two lines and subtract one from the other.
히든 1 = \"x가 띠의 왼쪽 끝보다 크다\", 히든 2 = \"x가: Hidden 1 = "x is past the band's left edge," hidden 2 = "x is past the band's right edge." Output = hidden 1 - hidden 2 turns on only between them.
값 조절: 히든 1은 x +3, 상시 -0.75(x ≈ 0.42부터 켜짐: Tuning: hidden 1 is x +3, always-on -0.75 (on from x ≈ 0.42). Hidden 2 is x +3, always-on -2 (fully on at x ≈ 0.83). At the output, hidden 2 must be subtracted hard at -2 so the orange on the right turns off. Change the activation function to "Step" and the boundary becomes razor-sharp.
x → 히든 1 +3, 상시 → 히든 1 -0.75, x → 히든 2 +: x → hidden 1 +3, always-on → hidden 1 -0.75, x → hidden 2 +3, always-on → hidden 2 -2, hidden 1 → output +1, hidden 2 → output -2.
파랑은 가운데 동그라미 안에, 주황은 그 바깥 고리에 있다. 히든 뉴런: Blue is inside a circle in the middle, orange in the ring around it. Use 4 hidden neurons to make one line each for top, bottom, left and right, and turn the output on only when all four lines say "inside." Combine enough lines and you can make any shape.
네 히든 뉴런을 \"x > 0.3\", \"x < 0.7\", \"y >: Make the four hidden neurons "x > 0.3", "x < 0.7", "y > 0.3", "y < 0.7". Turning on only when all four are true is AND.
값 조절: 히든 뉴런의 활성화 함수를 \"계단\"으로 바꾸면 0 아니면: Tuning: change the hidden neurons' activation function to "Step" and they output only 0 or 1. "x > 0.3" is x +3, always-on -0.4. "x < 0.7" is x -3, always-on +2.6. The output adds the four hidden neurons at +1 each with always-on -3 (1 only when all four are on).
히든 1~4를 계단 함수로: (x +3, 상시 -0.4) (x -3, 상: Hidden 1–4 as step functions: (x +3, always-on -0.4) (x -3, always-on +2.6) (y +3, always-on -0.4) (y -3, always-on +2.6) / hidden 1–4 → output +1, always-on → output -3.
훈련 데이터 22개 중 2개는 정답이 잘못 적혀 있다(실수로 붙은 꼬리표: 2 of the 22 training points have the wrong answer written on them (mislabeled by mistake). Real skill is measured with "test data" it has never seen. What happens if you force the boundary around even the wrong points to get the training data 100% right? The goal is 90% or more on the test data.
시험 데이터 90% 이상 맞히기: Get 90%+ of the test data right
잘못 적힌 두 점은 반대편 색들 한가운데 혼자 있다. 그 점에 맞추려고: The two mislabeled points sit alone in the middle of the opposite color. Twist the boundary to fit them and you get the nearby test data wrong. This is called overfitting (memorizing).
값 조절: 훈련 데이터는 2개를 틀려도(약 91%) 괜찮다. 단순한 대각: Tuning: it's fine to miss 2 training points (about 91%). A single simple diagonal (the same brain as in "A Slanted Line") gets the test data most right.
x → 출력 +1, y → 출력 +1, 상시 → 출력 -0.5. 히든 뉴: x → output +1, y → output +1, always-on → output -0.5. Don't use hidden neurons.
선을 스스로 찾기: Finding the Line on Its Own
이번에는 경계를 손으로 긋지 않는다. 엉뚱한 방향의 선에서 시작해서, 틀: This time you don't draw the boundary by hand. It starts from a line pointing the wrong way, and if it fixes the weights a little for each wrong point, the boundary turns by itself and finds its place. Watch how the background color changes with every round of learning.
모든 점을 맞히도록 스스로 배우게 하기: Let it learn to get every point right
학습 한 번 = 모든 점을 한 번씩 보고, 틀린 만큼 가중치를 고치는 것: One round of learning = look at every point once and fix the weights by how wrong it was. The same rule you used with truth tables in Chapter 4.
값 조절: 학습률 0.02면 25번, 0.1이면 7번, 0.3이면 5번: Tuning: at learning rate 0.02 it learns in 25 rounds, at 0.1 in 7, at 0.3 in 5. Big like 1 or 3, the boundary just swings wildly and never gets them all.
그림을 보는 AI(CNN)는 작은 3×3 \"필터\" 하나를 그림 위에서: An AI that sees pictures (CNN) moves a small 3×3 "filter" across the picture one cell at a time, repeating the same calculation. For each overlap, it adds up (picture cell × filter cell) and adds the bias, and that becomes one cell of the "feature map." Paint the filter so the feature map lights up only where there's a vertical line.
모든 그림에서 특징 맵이 목표와 같게: Make the feature map match the target in every picture
필터의 가운데 세로 세 칸에 +1을 칠하면, 세로줄과 겹칠 때 합이 3이: Paint +1 on the middle vertical three cells of the filter and the sum is 3 where it overlaps a vertical line. Other pictures (horizontal lines, diagonals) cross the middle column at only 1 cell.
값 조절: 합이 3일 때만 켜지려면 편향을 -2로 하자(3 - 2 = 1: Tuning: to light up only when the sum is 3, set the bias to -2 (3 - 2 = 1, 1 - 2 = negative). With bias 0, a diagonal or horizontal line lights it up just by crossing the middle at one cell, which is wrong; with -3 even the vertical line goes dark. -1 or -2 is right.
Middle vertical three cells of the filter +1, bias -2.
같은 그림이라도 필터를 바꾸면 전혀 다른 것을 찾는다. 이번에는 가로줄이: Even on the same picture, a different filter finds something completely different. This time make a filter that lights up only where there's a horizontal line. Real CNNs use tens to hundreds of filters like this together.
Just lay the vertical-line filter on its side.
Tuning: middle horizontal three cells +1, bias -2.
Middle horizontal three cells of the filter +1, bias -2.
이번에는 줄이 아니라 \"경계\"를 찾는다. 왼쪽이 어둡고 오른쪽이 밝아: This time you look for an "edge," not a line. Light up only where it's dark on the left and gets bright on the right. Human eyes and brains look for edges like this first, too.
왼쪽이 어둡고 오른쪽이 밝다 = \"오른쪽 칸은 더하고, 왼쪽 칸은 뺀다: Dark on the left, bright on the right = "add the right cells, subtract the left cells." In an all-bright picture, what you add and what you subtract are equal, so it becomes 0.
값 조절: 오른쪽 세로 세 칸 +1, 왼쪽 세로 세 칸 -1이면 경계 위: Tuning: right vertical three cells +1 and left vertical three cells -1 give a sum of 3 on the edge. Use bias -2 so it lights up only when the sum is 3. Leave the middle column at 0.
필터 왼쪽 세로 세 칸 -1, 오른쪽 세로 세 칸 +1, 가운데는 0,: Left vertical three cells of the filter -1, right vertical three cells +1, middle 0, bias -2.
이제 그림 전체를 분류한다. 필터 두 개(A, B)로 특징 맵을 만들고,: Now classify whole pictures. Make feature maps with two filters (A, B), and take just the single biggest value from each feature map (max pooling). Connect those two values to the output neuron and make it answer 1 for "a picture with only vertical lines" and 0 if there's any horizontal line. This is the whole flow of a CNN.
필터 A는 세로줄 찾기, 필터 B는 가로줄 찾기로 만들자. 풀링한 값은: Make filter A find vertical lines and filter B find horizontal lines. The pooled value then means "was that feature somewhere in the picture?"
값 조절: 출력 = A × (+1) + B × (-1) + 0. 세로만: Tuning: output = A × (+1) + B × (-1) + 0. Only vertical gives 1 - 0 = 1, only horizontal gives 0 - 1 → 0, both give 1 - 1 = 0.
필터 A = 가운데 세로 +1·편향 -2, 필터 B = 가운데 가로 +1: Filter A = middle vertical +1, bias -2; filter B = middle horizontal +1, bias -2; output: A +1, B -1, bias 0.
One neuron = one straight line on the plane.
The brain also looks at sensory information and sorts it into categories like "this is food, that is danger." Even as a stimulus changes little by little, there's a point where the judgment suddenly flips (a category boundary).
분류 AI는 입력 공간을 영역으로 나눈다. 영역이 바뀌는 곳이 결정 경계: A classifying AI divides the input space into regions. Where the region changes is the decision boundary. The decision boundary of a single neuron (perceptron) is always a straight line (a plane if there are many inputs). Fisher (1936) separated iris species with a "linear function": each measurement multiplied by a coefficient and added up. It's the classic of classification that draws the decision boundary as a straight line.
가중치와 편향의 모양: How Weights and Bias Shape It
The weights are the slope, the bias is the position.
뉴런의 문턱을 바꾸면 같은 자극에도 반응이 달라진다. 피곤하거나 긴장하면: Change a neuron's threshold and it reacts differently to the same stimulus. It's like how, when you're tired or tense, you react more easily (or less easily) to the same sound.
직선 w₁x + w₂y + b = 0.5에서 w₁:w₂의 비율이 선의 기: In the line w₁x + w₂y + b = 0.5, the ratio w₁:w₂ sets the line's slope and b sets its position. Learning comes down to turning and moving this line to fit the data. What Fisher (1936) found was also a coefficient to multiply each measurement by, which is the slope of the line.
시각 피질에서도 단순한 특징(선, 경계)을 보는 뉴런들의 신호가 모여,: In the visual cortex too, signals from neurons that see simple features (lines, edges) gather, and next-stage neurons recognize more complex shapes.
히든 뉴런 하나하나가 직선 경계를 하나씩 만들고, 출력 뉴런이 그것들을: Each hidden neuron makes one straight boundary, and the output neuron adds or subtracts them to make shapes like bands, squares and circles. The layer does what one straight line can't. Cybenko (1989) showed this as "superpositions of a sigmoidal function."
뇌의 뉴런 수는 엄청나게 많다. 단순한 계산을 하는 뉴런을 아주 많이 모: The brain has an enormous number of neurons. Gather a huge number of neurons doing simple calculations and you can make complex judgments.
히든층이 하나만 있어도 히든 뉴런이 충분히 많으면 원하는 모양을 얼마든지: It's known that even with a single hidden layer, enough hidden neurons can get as close as you like to any shape you want (the universal approximation theorem). Wrapping a circle in a square is the first step. Hornik and colleagues (1989) showed, just as their paper's title says, that multilayer networks are "universal approximators."
시험 문제를 통째로 외우면 같은 문제는 맞히지만 조금 바뀐 문제는 틀린다: Memorize the test questions whole and you'll get the same questions right but slightly changed ones wrong. You have to understand the principle to solve problems you've never seen.
AI는 훈련 데이터로 배우고, 처음 보는 시험 데이터로 실력을 잰다. 훈: An AI learns from training data and is measured on test data it has never seen. Getting too complex in order to fit even the mistakes (noise) in the training data is called overfitting; doing well on unseen data is called generalization. Zhang and colleagues (2016) showed that neural networks can memorize even "random labels," and Srivastava and colleagues (2014) introduced "dropout" to reduce "overfitting."
Rolling downhill a little at a time.
뇌는 한 번에 완벽하게 배우지 않는다. 연습할 때마다 조금씩 고쳐 나가면: The brain doesn't learn perfectly in one go. It fixes a little with each practice, and the mistakes shrink.
오차가 줄어드는 방향으로 가중치를 조금씩 옮기는 것을 경사 하강법이라고: Moving the weights little by little in the direction that reduces the error is called gradient descent. If you picture the error as a mountain, it's like stepping down the steepest way one step at a time. Almost every neural network learns this way. Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams (1986) also used "gradient descent" to reduce the error. Its mathematical root is Robbins and Monro's (1951) "stochastic approximation."
One small filter moved across the whole picture.
1959년 휴벨과 비셀은 고양이 시각 피질에서 특정 방향의 선에만 반응하: In 1959 Hubel and Wiesel found neurons in the cat's visual cortex that respond only to lines at a particular angle (Nobel Prize, 1981). Each neuron sees only a small part of the visual field.
합성곱 신경망(CNN)은 3×3 같은 작은 필터를 그림의 모든 자리에 똑: A convolutional neural network (CNN) applies a small filter, such as 3×3, the same way at every spot in the picture (weight sharing). So the same filter can find a line wherever it is in the picture, and very few weights are needed. Hubel and Wiesel (1959) called the small part of the visual field one neuron sees its "receptive field." LeCun and colleagues (1989) called using the same filter everywhere "weight sharing."
시각 피질에는 세로선, 가로선, 비스듬한 선에 각각 반응하는 뉴런들이 따: The visual cortex has separate neurons that respond to vertical, horizontal and slanted lines. It sees the same scene from several "viewpoints" at once.
필터 하나가 만든 결과를 특징 맵이라고 한다. CNN은 필터 수십~수백: The result made by one filter is called a feature map. A CNN makes many feature maps with tens to hundreds of filters, and the next layer takes those feature maps as input to find more complex features. Hubel and Wiesel (1962) distinguished "simple cells," which respond to simple lines, from "complex cells," which respond even if the position shifts a little. Fukushima's (1980) neocognitron borrowed these names, alternating layers of "S-cells" that find features and "C-cells" that gather them.
눈의 망막과 시각 피질의 첫 단계는 밝기가 갑자기 바뀌는 경계에 특히 강: The retina and the first stage of the visual cortex react especially strongly to edges where brightness changes suddenly. That's why we can tell what a picture is from just a few lines.
\"한쪽은 빼고 한쪽은 더하는\" 필터는 경계를 찾는다. 사진 편집의 가: A filter that "subtracts one side and adds the other" finds edges. Edge detection in photo editing works the same way. The first-layer filters of a trained CNN also take on this edge-filter shape all by themselves. Marr and Hildreth (1980) built a theory of "edge detection" that finds edges where the change in brightness flips sign, the "zero-crossings."
When whether it was there matters more than where.
Neurons in deeper stages of the visual cortex respond wherever the object is in the visual field. It's the ability to recognize the same object even if its position shifts a little.
최대 풀링은 특징 맵에서 가장 큰 값만 남겨 \"이 특징이 어딘가에 있었: Max pooling keeps only the biggest value of a feature map and passes on just "this feature was somewhere." The structure of convolution → pooling → classification is a CNN; LeNet-5, which read handwritten digits in 1998, and AlexNet, which classified photos into 1000 kinds in 2012, both had this structure. LeCun and colleagues' (1998) LeNet-5 called this layer "subsampling" and used the average instead of the maximum. Pooling with the maximum became widespread later, like AlexNet's (2012) "overlapping pooling."
지금까지의 뇌는 지금 들어온 입력만 보고 답했다. 이번에는 입력이 한 칸: Until now the brain answered by looking only at the input coming in now. This time the inputs come in one cell at a time, in time order, and the output must say "the input from the previous cell." You can never tell from the current input alone. The memory 1 neuron brings back the value hidden 1 gave in the previous cell. This feedback is the heart of a recurrent neural network (RNN).
모든 칸에서 출력 = 바로 전 칸의 입력: In every cell, output = the input from the previous cell
히든 1에 지금 입력을 담아 두면, 다음 칸에서 기억 1로 돌아온다. 먼: Store the current input in hidden 1 and it comes back as memory 1 in the next cell. First connect input A → hidden 1.
값 조절: 히든 1은 입력 A를 그대로(+1) 받으면 된다. 출력은 지금: Tuning: hidden 1 just takes input A as is (+1). The output must answer by looking only at memory 1, not the current input, so memory 1 → output +1. If you also connect input A to the output, "now" gets mixed in and it's wrong.
입력이 한 번이라도 1이 된 적이 있으면, 그 뒤로는 끝까지 1을 말해야: If the input has ever been 1 even once, from then on it must say 1 until the end. This time there's an output memory neuron. The value the output gave in the previous cell comes back to itself. How do you wire it to hold on to something once it's on?
출력 = \"지금 입력이 1\" 또는 \"바로 전에 이미 켜져 있었음\": Output = "the current input is 1" or "it was already on just before." For OR, just add the two lines.
값 조절: 입력 A → 출력 +1, 출력 기억 → 출력 +1. 한 번 1: Tuning: input A → output +1, output memory → output +1. Once it becomes 1, the output memory comes back as 1 in the next cell and it stays on. If the output memory's strength is below 1 (e.g. 0.8), the memory shrinks every cell, 0.8 → 0.64 → 0.51 → 0.41 …, and eventually goes out. The strength has to be 1 to hold on until the end.
Input A → output +1, output memory → output +1.
입력이 두 칸 연속으로 1일 때만 출력을 켜자. \"지금 1\"이고 \": Turn the output on only when the input is 1 two cells in a row. It has to be "1 now" and "1 just before too." Even for the same input 1, the answer depends on what came before. Add memory to the AND from Chapter 1.
두 칸 연속 1일 때만 출력 1: Output 1 only after two 1s in a row
첫 실험처럼 히든 1에 지금 입력을 담아 두면 다음 칸에 기억 1로 돌아: As in the first experiment, store the current input in hidden 1 and it comes back as memory 1 in the next cell. Output = current input AND memory 1.
값 조절: AND는 두 선을 +1씩 더하고 상시 -1을 주면 된다. 둘: Tuning: for AND, add the two lines at +1 each and give always-on -1. Both 1 gives 1 + 1 - 1 = 1; only one 1 gives 0.
입력 A → 히든 1 +1, 입력 A → 출력 +1, 기억 1 → 출력: Input A → hidden 1 +1, input A → output +1, memory 1 → output +1, always-on → output -1.
이번에는 두 칸 전의 입력을 말해야 한다. 그런데 기억은 바로 한 칸 전: This time it must say the input from two cells ago. But memory only brings back the value from one cell earlier. To remember longer, the memory has to be handed on from neuron to neuron. Hidden 1 → memory 1 → hidden 2 → memory 2.
모든 칸에서 출력 = 두 칸 전의 입력: In every cell, output = the input from two cells ago
히든 1에는 지금 입력을, 히든 2에는 기억 1(= 한 칸 전 입력)을: Put the current input in hidden 1 and memory 1 (= the input one cell ago) in hidden 2. Then memory 2 becomes the input from two cells ago.
값 조절: 모두 +1로 그대로 넘기면 된다. 세기를 1보다 작게 하면 넘: Tuning: just pass everything on at +1. If the strength is below 1, the value shrinks every time it's passed (0.8 × 0.8 = 0.64). Pass it through dozens of cells and the memory nearly vanishes. That's why very long memories are hard, and why structures like LSTM came about.
입력 A → 히든 1 +1, 기억 1 → 히든 2 +1, 기억 2 → 출: Input A → hidden 1 +1, memory 1 → hidden 2 +1, memory 2 → output +1.
지금까지 1이 몇 번 들어왔는지 세어서, 홀수 번이면 1, 짝수 번이면: Count how many 1s have come in so far, and say 1 if it's odd and 0 if it's even. You don't need to count forever. You only need to remember one thing: "has it been odd so far?" Every new 1 flips the answer.
지금까지 1이 홀수 번이면 1: 1 if 1 has come in an odd number of times so far
New answer = current input XOR output memory. It's 1 when only one of the two is 1. Use two hidden neurons, like the XOR in Chapter 1.
값 조절: 히든 1 = 입력 A +1, 출력 기억 -1(\"입력만 1\": Tuning: hidden 1 = input A +1, output memory -1 ("only the input is 1"). Hidden 2 = output memory +1, input A -1 ("only the memory is 1"). Output = hidden 1 + hidden 2.
입력 A → 히든 1 +1, 출력 기억 → 히든 1 -1, 출력 기억 →: Input A → hidden 1 +1, output memory → hidden 1 -1, output memory → hidden 2 +1, input A → hidden 2 -1, hidden 1 → output +1, hidden 2 → output +1.
이번 점들에는 색(정답)이 없다. 정답 없이 데이터 속에서 비슷한 것끼리: These points have no color (answer). Grouping similar things in data without answers is called unsupervised learning. The two big circles are "centers," and each point takes the color of the nearest center. Drag the centers so the two groups you can see end up in different colors.
두 무리를 서로 다른 색으로 묶기: Group the two clusters in different colors
점들이 왼쪽 위와 오른쪽 아래, 두 덩어리로 모여 있다. 중심을 하나씩: The points gather in two clumps, top left and bottom right. Drag one center into each clump.
값 조절: \"거리 합\"은 모든 점과 자기 중심 사이 거리(제곱)를 더: Tuning: the "distance sum" adds up the (squared) distance between every point and its center. The closer the centers are to the middle of the clumps, the smaller it gets. The smallest possible is {0}; to get all the stars, {1} or less.
중심 하나는 왼쪽 위 덩어리 한가운데, 다른 하나는 오른쪽 아래 덩어리: Put one center in the middle of the top-left clump and the other in the middle of the bottom-right clump.
이번에는 중심을 손으로 옮길 수 없다. 대신 \"한 걸음\" 버튼이 있다: This time you can't move the centers by hand. Instead there's a "One step" button. One step has two stages. ① Group: each point takes the color of the nearest center. ② Move: each center goes to the middle (average) of the points of its color. Repeating until the centers stop moving is the k-means algorithm.
세 무리를 찾고 중심이 멈출 때까지: Find the three clusters, until the centers stop
\"한 걸음\"을 눌러 보자. 점선 화살표 끝은 다음 걸음에 중심이 갈: Press "One step." The tip of the dotted arrow is where the center will go next step (the average of the points of its color).
값 조절: 중심이 더 움직이지 않으면 상태가 \"멈춤\"으로 바뀐다. 이: Tuning: when the centers stop moving, the status changes to "Stopped." This data stops in 3 steps. Also watch the distance sum shrink with every step.
\"한 걸음\"을 세 번(또는 \"멈출 때까지\"를 한 번) 누르고 채점: Press "One step" three times (or "Until it stops" once) and check.
이번에도 무리는 셋이다. 그런데 이대로 걸으면 중심 둘이 오른쪽 위 무리: There are three clusters this time too. But if you just step, two centers split the top-right cluster between them, and one center ends up stuck covering both bottom clusters. k-means can get trapped in a wrong answer depending on where it starts (a local minimum). You can drag the centers. Fix the starting spots.
세 무리를 제대로 찾고 중심이 멈출 때까지: Find the three clusters properly, until the centers stop
먼저 \"멈출 때까지\"를 눌러 어디에 갇히는지 보자. 그다음 \"처음: First press "Until it stops" to see where it gets trapped. Then press "Back to start" and change the starting spots.
값 조절: 갇히면 거리 합이 {0}에서 더 줄지 않는다. 오른쪽 위에 몰: Tuning: when trapped, the distance sum won't go below {0}. Move one of the centers crowded in the top right to one of the two bottom clusters, then step, and it drops to {1}.
\"처음 자리로\" → 오른쪽 위 중심 하나를 왼쪽 아래 무리 한가운데로: "Back to start" → drag one top-right center to the middle of the bottom-left cluster → "Until it stops."
마지막은 무리가 몇 개인지도 정해야 한다. 중심 수(k)를 1~6 중에: Last, you also have to decide how many clusters there are. You can pick the number of centers (k) from 1 to 6. Change k and step until it stops, and a "distance sum per k" bar piles up for each. As k grows, the distance sum drops a lot, then at some point barely drops at all. That bend (the elbow) is the right number of clusters.
알맞은 무리 수로 무리를 찾고 멈출 때까지: Find the clusters with the right number, until it stops

값 조절: k = 3이면 거리 합이 {0}, 4면 {1}로 확 줄고, 5: Tuning: at k = 3 the distance sum is {0}, at 4 it drops sharply to {1}, and from 5 it stays about the same ({2}). Make k bigger than the number of clusters and the distance sum shrinks, but it forces a cluster to split. The elbow is k = 4.
이번 뇌는 입력을 그대로 다시 그려 내야 한다. A가 켜지면 출력 1을,: This brain has to redraw its input exactly. When A is on, turn on output 1; when B is on, turn on output 2. Looks easy, but there's a condition. You can't connect inputs straight to outputs; they must pass through one hidden neuron in the middle (the code). The part that shrinks information into a small code is the encoder, and the part that brings it back from the code is the decoder.
히든 뉴런 하나를 거쳐 입력을 그대로 살리기: Restore the input through one hidden neuron
Write "A or B?" with one code. Hidden 1 = 1 for A, 0 for B.

입력 A → 히든 1 +1, 히든 1 → 출력 +1, 히든 1 → 출력: Input A → hidden 1 +1, hidden 1 → output +1, hidden 1 → output 2 -1, always-on → output 2 +1.
입력 넷 중 하나만 켜진다. 이것을 히든 뉴런 둘(코드 두 칸)로 줄였다: Only one of the four inputs is on. Shrink it into two hidden neurons (two code cells), then bring it back to four. Two code cells can make exactly four combinations: 00, 10, 01, 11. Give each input a different combination. In the "code map" below, check that the four inputs land in different corners.

Keep only "which pattern is it closer to?" as a code in one hidden neuron, and let the decoder redraw the clean pattern. Noise can't squeeze through a small code.

Nobody sets the code, yet once it has learned, the two hidden neurons give the four inputs different codes. Watch the code map.
스스로 배워 네 입력을 모두 살리기: Learn on its own to restore all four inputs
학습률을 고르고 자동 학습을 누르자. 코드 지도에서 네 점이 서로 다른: Pick a learning rate and press Auto-learn. Watch the four points scatter to different corners of the code map.
값 조절: 학습률 0.02면 248번, 0.1이면 45번, 0.3이면 9: Tuning: at learning rate 0.02 it learns in 248 rounds, at 0.1 in 45, at 0.3 in 9, at 0.5 in 8. At 1 or more it's too big and never gets them all.
Today's me listens to yesterday's me.
뇌의 회로는 한 방향으로만 흐르지 않는다. 신호가 다시 앞쪽으로 되돌아오: Brain circuits don't flow in only one direction. There are a great many loops where signals come back toward the front (feedback), and thanks to these loops the brain can briefly hold on to what it just saw (working memory).
순환 신경망(RNN)은 히든 뉴런의 값을 다음 순간의 입력으로 함께 넣는: A recurrent neural network (RNN) feeds the hidden neurons' values back in as input at the next moment. That lets it handle data with a time order, like sentences, sounds and sensor readings. It reuses the same weights at every step. Elman (1990) called the neurons that take back the hidden values "context units." Those are the memory neurons in this game.
Once on, it keeps itself on.
자기 자신을 다시 흥분시키는 뉴런 무리는 자극이 사라진 뒤에도 계속 발화: A group of neurons that re-excites itself keeps firing even after the stimulus is gone. This kind of sustained firing is seen in the prefrontal cortex while you briefly hold a phone number in mind.
출력을 자기 자신에게 되먹이면 한 번 켜진 값을 붙잡는 \"기억 소자\": Feed the output back to itself and it becomes a "memory element" that holds on to a value once it's on. The basic circuits of computer memory (latches, flip-flops) work the same way. If the feedback is weak, the memory fades. Fuster and Alexander (1971) found such neurons in the monkey brain and linked them to "short-term memory." Hopfield (1982) called it "content-addressable memory" when a feedback network settles into a stable state and recalls a memory.
The same 1, depending on what came before.
\"사과\"와 \"과사\"는 같은 글자인데 뜻이 다르다. 뇌는 소리와 글: "Dog" and "god" use the same letters but mean different things. The brain takes in sounds and letters in order and interprets the current one differently depending on what came before.
시간 순서가 있는 데이터를 시퀀스라고 한다. 시퀀스 모델은 지금 입력과: Data with a time order is called a sequence. A sequence model answers by looking at the current input together with its memory so far (the hidden state). Speech recognition, weather forecasting and spotting fault signals in machines are all sequence problems. Elman (1990) showed, just as his paper's title says, that recurrent networks find "structure in time."
It blurs a little every time it's passed on.
방금 들은 말은 또렷하지만 몇 분 전 말은 흐릿하다. 뇌는 오래 남길 것: What you just heard is clear, but words from a few minutes ago are fuzzy. The brain picks out what to keep for long and moves it into long-term memory by way of the hippocampus.
A basic RNN passes memory along every step, and the value keeps shrinking or blowing up. During learning too, the gradient that carries the error back to the distant past gets multiplied at every step and either vanishes to 0 (the vanishing gradient) or explodes, so it can't learn the distant past well. LSTM, introduced in 1997, solved this by adding gates that decide "keep the memory as is, or erase it." Bengio and colleagues (1994) showed this as the difficulty of learning "long-term dependencies," and LSTM (Hochreiter and Schmidhuber 1997) solved it with a "constant error carousel" that carries the error without shrinking.
You don't have to remember everything. Just what you need.
계단을 오를 때 몇 칸째인지 다 기억하지 않아도 \"왼발 차례인지 오른발: Climbing stairs, you don't remember which step you're on; you walk fine just knowing "is it the left foot's turn or the right?" The brain carries around only the summary it needs, as a state.
RNN의 은닉 상태는 지금까지의 입력 전체를 요약한 값이다. 홀짝 세기는: An RNN's hidden state is a summary of all the input so far. Odd-or-even counting handles input of any length with just one state (has it been odd so far?) and XOR. A machine that runs on "state + rules" like this is called a state machine. Elman (1990), with the same idea, had a recurrent network solve "temporal XOR," where 1s come in one cell at a time.
아기는 누가 알려 주지 않아도 엄마 목소리와 다른 소리를, 고양이와 개를: Without anyone telling them, babies group mom's voice apart from other sounds, and cats apart from dogs. Look at enough things and similar ones group themselves.
Finding structure in data without answers (labels) is called unsupervised learning. Clustering, which groups similar things, is the classic example. It's used when an online store sorts customers into similar groups, or when photos are organized by similarity. Rumelhart and Zipser (1985) found features without answers through "competitive learning," where only the best-matching neuron wins and learns.
뇌에도 비슷한 입력에 서로 먼저 반응하려고 경쟁하는 뉴런들이 있다. 가장: The brain also has neurons that compete to respond first to similar inputs. The best-matching neuron wins, and the winner tunes itself a little more toward that input (competitive learning).
k-평균은 ① 점마다 가장 가까운 중심에 묶고 ② 중심을 자기 점들의 평: k-means repeats ① group each point with its nearest center and ② move each center to the average of its points. The distance sum shrinks every step and it finally stops. If you see each center as a neuron with two weights (x, y), it's the same as competitive learning where only the nearest neuron wins. Lloyd (1957 report, published 1982) solved this as a "quantization" problem, storing a signal with a small number of values. The name "k-means" was given by MacQueen (1967).
한 번 익힌 습관은 더 좋은 방법이 있어도 잘 바뀌지 않는다. 처음 길을: A habit, once learned, doesn't change easily even when there's a better way. How you first wore the path lasts a long time.
학습은 비용(거리 합, 오차)이 줄어드는 쪽으로만 움직이기 때문에, 근처: Because learning only moves in the direction that lowers the cost (distance sum, error), once it falls into the lowest valley nearby, it can't get to a deeper valley even if one exists. That's a local minimum. So people try several starting spots and pick the best answer, or choose starting centers that are far apart from each other. The latter is Arthur and Vassilvitskii's (2007) k-means++, which the paper calls "careful seeding."
친구들을 \"가까운 친구 / 아는 사람\"으로 나누는 것과 100가지로: Splitting your friends into "close friends / acquaintances" versus splitting them 100 ways: a classification that's too fine is hard to remember and hard to use.
중심 수 k를 늘리면 거리 합은 언제나 줄어든다(점마다 중심을 주면 0): Raising the number of centers k always lowers the distance sum (one center per point gives 0). So you pick as the right k the spot where the distance sum drops a lot and then suddenly drops less, where the graph bends: the "elbow." The trap where a more complex model always looks better is the same story as overfitting in Chapter 6. Thorndike (1953) first used the method of changing the number of clusters and finding the bend in the graph where the scatter shrinks.
Shrink it, then bring it back.
눈에서 뇌로 가는 시신경 섬유는 약 100만 가닥으로, 빛을 받는 시세포: The optic nerve from eye to brain has about 1 million fibers, far fewer than the light-sensing cells (more than 100 million). The eye doesn't send what it sees as is; it sends a summary (compression).
오토인코더는 입력을 작은 코드로 줄이는 인코더와, 코드에서 입력을 다시: An autoencoder is a neural network made of an encoder that shrinks the input into a small code and a decoder that redraws the input from the code. It learns with "the input itself" as the target instead of an answer, so it needs no labels. Hinton and Salakhutdinov (2006) split a network narrow in the middle into an "encoder" and a "decoder," trained it to restore its input, and so achieved "reducing the dimensionality" of data.
A place on the code map.
해마의 장소 세포와 격자 세포는 수많은 감각 정보를 \"지도 위의 자리\: Place cells and grid cells in the hippocampus turn huge amounts of sensory information into a small code: "a place on the map."
코드 값들이 놓이는 공간을 잠재 공간이라고 한다. 잘 배운 잠재 공간에서: The space where code values sit is called the latent space. In a well-learned latent space, similar things sit close together. Turning words and photos into bundles of numbers (embeddings), and image-generating AI drawing new pictures from codes, both came from this idea. Kingma and Welling (2013) call the code a "latent variable." Place cells were found by O'Keefe and Dostrovsky (1971), and "grid cells" by Hafting and colleagues (2005).
Noise can't get through a narrow door.
시끄러운 곳에서도 아는 사람의 말소리는 알아듣는다. 뇌는 귀에 들어온 소: Even in a noisy place, you can make out the voice of someone you know. The brain doesn't trust the sound reaching the ear as is; it fills in gaps to match patterns it knows and filters out noise.
잡음 섞인 입력에서 깨끗한 원본을 살리도록 배운 것을 디노이징 오토인코더: A network trained to restore the clean original from noisy input is called a denoising autoencoder. If the code is small, only "the important pattern" fits, and there's no room for noise. Photo restoration and image-generating AI (diffusion models) also learn to strip away noise. Vincent and colleagues (2008) introduced the "denoising autoencoder," which learns to restore the original from deliberately damaged (corrupted) input, and Ho and colleagues' (2020) "denoising diffusion" models became the basis of image generation.
Through repeated experience, the brain builds for itself what to represent and how (representations). We get used to new faces quickly because we've already learned good representations for faces.
역전파는 출력만 맞추라고 했을 뿐인데, 히든 뉴런에는 입력을 구별하는 코: Backpropagation was only told to get the output right, yet a code that tells inputs apart appears in the hidden neurons by itself. Finding useful representations on its own is called representation learning, and most of today's AI power comes from here. Bengio, Courville and Vincent (2013) summed this up as "representation learning," and Mikolov and colleagues (2013) learned "word representations in vector space."
뉴런 하나(출력 = w × 입력 + b)가 점 네 개를 지나는 직선을 맞: A single neuron (output = w × input + b) tries to fit a line through four points. Put weight w across and bias b up and down, color every spot by its error, and you get an "error landscape." The darker the spot, the smaller the error. Learning (gradient descent) moves the ball one step at a time in the steepest downhill direction from where it is. The learning rate is the size of one step. Stop the ball at the bottom (the gold circle).
공을 바닥(금색 원)에 멈추게 하기: Stop the ball at the bottom (gold circle)
학습률이 너무 작으면 공이 아주 천천히 내려가서 100걸음 안에 바닥에: If the learning rate is too small, the ball rolls down very slowly and can't reach the bottom within 100 steps. Too big and it flies out across the valley.
값 조절: 학습률 0.05면 100걸음 안에 못 닿고, 0.1이면 53걸: Tuning: at learning rate 0.05 it can't reach it within 100 steps; at 0.1 it stops in 53 steps, at 0.2 in 26. From 0.3 the steps are too big and it flies off the landscape.
이번 지형은 한쪽으로 길고 좁은 골짜기다. 두 입력의 크기가 아주 다르면: This landscape is a long, narrow valley stretched one way. It appears when two inputs are very different in size (e.g. height 170, age 15). Gradient descent just zigzags between the steep walls and barely gets toward the bottom. Momentum remembers the speed of past steps and adds a force (inertia) that keeps going the same way. β is how much speed it remembers.
80걸음 안에 공을 바닥에 멈추게 하기: Stop the ball at the bottom within 80 steps
경사 하강으로는 학습률을 어떻게 골라도 80걸음 안에 못 닿는다(0.5는: With gradient descent, no learning rate reaches it within 80 steps (0.5 flies off). Switch the optimizer to momentum.
값 조절: 모멘텀 β 0.9면 학습률 0.05에서 55걸음, 0.3에서: Tuning: with momentum β 0.9, learning rate 0.05 takes 55 steps and 0.3 takes 58. With β 0.5 and learning rate 0.5 it gets there in 36. A big β means lots of inertia, so it overshoots the bottom and comes back.
"Until it stops" with momentum, β 0.5, learning rate 0.5.
이번 지형에는 깊은 바닥(금색 원) 말고도 출발점 가까이에 작은 웅덩이가: Besides the deep bottom (gold circle), this landscape has a small puddle near the start. Gradient descent only looks at "the downhill direction right under my feet," so once it falls into the puddle it thinks that's the bottom and stops (a local minimum). Get over the puddle with inertia, or move the start point. You can drag the start point (white circle).
깊은 바닥(금색 원)에 공을 멈추게 하기: Stop the ball at the deep bottom (gold circle)
먼저 경사 하강으로 \"멈출 때까지\"를 눌러 어디에 갇히는지 보자. 경: First press "Until it stops" with gradient descent to see where it gets trapped. Gradient descent can't escape the small puddle at any learning rate.
값 조절: 모멘텀 β 0.9에 학습률 0.3이면 52걸음, 0.5면 50: Tuning: with momentum β 0.9 and learning rate 0.3 it crosses the puddle and reaches the deep bottom in 52 steps, at 0.5 in 50. β 0.5 doesn't have enough inertia and stays in the puddle. Move the start point toward the deep valley (top right) and even gradient descent works.
출발점은 그대로 두고 모멘텀, β 0.9, 학습률 0.5로 \"멈출 때까: Leave the start point as is, and "Until it stops" with momentum, β 0.9, learning rate 0.5.
이번 지형은 가로로는 아주 가파르고 세로로는 거의 평평하다. 학습률 하나: This landscape is very steep across and almost flat up and down. One learning rate can't suit both. Make it big and it flies off on the steep side; make it small and it crawls on the flat side. Adam remembers the size of the gradient so far for each weight and sets each step size separately. It's the most widely used method for training neural networks today.
경사 하강과 모멘텀은 어떤 학습률로도 80걸음 안에 못 닿는다. 세로 방: Gradient descent and momentum can't reach it within 80 steps at any learning rate. The up-and-down gradient is just too small.
값 조절: Adam은 기울기를 그 크기로 나눠서 쓰기 때문에 평평한 쪽에: Tuning: Adam divides the gradient by its size, so even on the flat side it moves steadily by about the learning rate. Learning rate 0.1 takes 63 steps, 0.2 takes 59, 0.3 takes 60, 0.5 takes 65.
"Until it stops" with Adam, learning rate 0.2.
5장에서는 행동마다 점수를 줬다. 이번에는 \"이 칸에 있으면 앞으로 점: In Chapter 5 you gave points for actions. This time you write in each cell "how many points will I get from here on if I'm in this cell?" That's value. Value is the best of "the reward for one step + discount γ × the value of the cell you arrive at" (the Bellman equation). Each spread pushes value out one cell further from the goal (+10). Once value reaches the start cell, you just follow the arrows.
출발에서 화살표를 따라 목표까지 가기: Follow the arrows from the start to the goal
\"한 번 퍼뜨리기\"를 누를 때마다 가치가 목표에서 한 칸씩 멀리 번진: Every time you press "Spread once," value spreads one cell further from the goal.
값 조절: 출발에서 목표까지 가장 짧은 길은 15걸음이라서 14번 퍼뜨리: Tuning: the shortest path from start to goal is 15 steps, so after 14 spreads value reaches the cell next to the start and the path connects. Because γ is 0.9, value shrinks to 0.9 times for each cell further from the goal.
출발 가까이에 작은 보상(+1), 멀리에 큰 보상(+10)이 있다. 할인: There's a small reward (+1) near the start and a big reward (+10) far away. The discount γ is "how much is a reward you get later worth now?" With a small γ it picks the small reward right in front of it; with a big γ, the big reward far away. Make the arrows head for the big reward (+10). Changing γ spreads the value again from scratch.
화살표가 큰 보상(+10)으로 가게 하기: Make the arrows head for the big reward (+10)
작은 보상은 2걸음, 큰 보상은 7걸음 떨어져 있다. 큰 보상의 가치는: The small reward is 2 steps away, the big reward 7. The value of the big reward shrinks by γ times with every step.
값 조절: 출발에서 보면 작은 보상은 1 × γ, 큰 보상은 10 × γ: Tuning: seen from the start, the small reward is worth 1 × γ and the big reward 10 × γ⁶. For 10 × γ⁶ to be bigger, γ⁵ > 0.1, so γ must be above about 0.63. That's why 0.5 and 0.6 go to the small reward, and from 0.7 it goes to the big one. Value needs at least 6 spreads to reach the start.
Change γ to 0.7, press "Spread once" 6 or more times, then check.
이번에는 지도를 모른다. 가치를 미리 계산할 수 없으니 직접 돌아다니며: This time you don't know the map. Value can't be computed in advance, so it learns by moving around (Q-learning). Each cell keeps a score table (Q) for its four directions, and with every step it nudges Q toward "the reward received + γ × the best Q of the cell it arrived at." Every step costs -1, so wandering around longer is a loss. Make it learn the shortest path.
가장 짧은 길(9걸음)로 목표까지 가게 배우기: Learn to reach the goal by the shortest path (9 steps)
\"한 판 해 보기\"를 눌러 몇 판 돌려 보자. 판이 쌓일수록 칸의 숫: Press "Play one episode" and run a few. As episodes pile up, the numbers and arrows in the cells line up toward the goal.

Learning is a ball rolling down into a valley.
뇌의 시냅스 세기도 경험할 때마다 조금씩 바뀐다. 어떤 바뀜이 더 나은: Synapse strengths in the brain also change a little with every experience. Exactly how the brain knows which changes make better behavior isn't fully understood yet.
가중치마다 축을 하나씩 두고 오차를 높이로 놓으면 지형이 된다. 경사 하: Give each weight its own axis and put the error as height, and you get a landscape. Gradient descent repeats: measure the slope where you are, and move by the learning rate in the steepest downhill direction. Real neural networks have billions of weights, so their landscapes have billions of dimensions. Li and colleagues (2018) drew the "loss landscape" of real neural networks and showed that the wider and flatter the bottom, the better they do on unseen data (generalization).
A rolling ball doesn't stop easily.
운동을 배울 때도 매번 처음부터 고치기보다, 잘되던 방향으로 계속 다듬어: When you learn a movement, rather than fixing it from scratch each time, you keep refining in the direction that was working.
모멘텀은 지난 걸음들의 방향을 평균 내어 \"속도\"로 기억하고, 그 속: Momentum averages the directions of past steps, remembers it as a "velocity," and moves at that velocity. Zigzagging directions cancel each other out, and steady directions pile up, so it gets through narrow valleys quickly. The bigger β is, the longer it remembers. Polyak (1964) called this the "heavy ball" method, and Sutskever and colleagues (2013) showed how important "momentum" is for training deep neural networks.
If you only look at your feet, a puddle looks like the bottom.
When a familiar way is "good enough," you stop looking for a better one. You have to try something different now and then to find a better place.
경사 하강은 근처의 오목한 곳(지역 최소)에 멈출 수 있다. 관성(모멘텀: Gradient descent can stop in a nearby dip (local minimum). Inertia (momentum), changing the starting values, and noise mixed into learning (mini-batches) help it escape small puddles. But in real networks with huge numbers of dimensions, flat saddle points are known to be a bigger problem than puddles. Dauphin and colleagues (2014) showed that with very many dimensions, "saddle points" slow learning down more than puddles do.
A separate step size for each weight.
뇌의 시냅스도 저마다 바뀌는 속도가 다르다. 자주 쓰이는 연결과 드물게: Synapses in the brain also each change at their own speed. Connections used often and connections used rarely are tuned differently.
Adam은 가중치마다 기울기의 평균(모멘텀)과 기울기 크기의 평균을 따로: Adam remembers, separately for each weight, the average of the gradient (momentum) and the average size of the gradient, and decides each step by dividing the gradient by its size. So it moves at a similar size on both the steep side and the flat side. It came out in 2014 and is now the most widely used. Adam is short for "adaptive moment estimation" (Kingma and Ba 2014). The idea of dividing each weight's step by its gradient size came from Duchi and colleagues' (2011) AdaGrad.
How good will it be from here on?
원숭이 실험에서 \"곧 보상이 온다\"는 신호(불빛·소리)를 익히고 나면: In monkey experiments, once the animals learn a signal (a light, a sound) that means "a reward is coming soon," dopamine neurons respond to that signal first, before the reward itself. The brain also computes a prediction that "something good is coming," in other words, value.
가치는 어떤 상태에서 시작해 앞으로 받을 보상의 합이다. 벨만 방정식은: Value is the sum of rewards you'll get from here on, starting from a given state. The Bellman equation links value from cell to cell: "value now = reward for one step + γ × value of the next state." Once you know the values, you just go toward the highest one. Bellman (1952) founded "dynamic programming," which breaks a big problem into "one step now + the rest of the problem." Schultz and colleagues (1997) showed that dopamine neurons send a reward "prediction error."
What are tomorrow's 10 points worth today?
사람과 동물은 나중에 받을 보상을 더 작게 느낀다(시간 할인). 지금 과: People and animals feel rewards that come later as smaller (time discounting). Agonizing between one cookie now and two cookies a week later is an example.
할인율 γ(0~1)는 한 걸음 늦게 받는 보상에 곱하는 값이다. γ가 작: The discount γ (0–1) is the number you multiply a reward by for each step it comes later. With a small γ it only sees the reward right in front; close to 1, it sees far into the future. Keeping γ below 1 also makes the sum of endlessly continuing rewards finite. Sutton and Barto (2018) call γ the "discount rate." The idea of shaving future satisfaction by a fixed rate and adding it up came from economist Samuelson's (1937) discounted utility model.
Value learned by doing, without a map.
처음 가는 동네에서도 이리저리 다녀 보며 어느 길이 빠른지 익힌다. 결과: Even in a neighborhood you've never been to, you wander around and learn which way is fastest. If the result is better than expected, you trust that choice more.
Q러닝은 상태마다 행동별 점수 Q를 두고, 한 걸음 갈 때마다 \"받은: Q-learning keeps a score Q for each action in each state, and with every step it fixes Q by the difference from "reward received + γ × the best Q of the next state." It learns even without knowing the rules of the world. In 2015 DQN replaced this Q with a neural network and learned Atari games. Watkins and Dayan (1992) called Q the "action-value" and proved that if every action is tried enough, Q converges to the best values. DQN (Mnih and colleagues 2015) is a "deep Q-network."
When groups of neurons compete by suppressing each other, only the strongest remains large. This kind of competition is thought to happen when the brain picks one of several interpretations.
소프트맥스는 각 출력의 지수(e^값)를 전체 합으로 나눠, 모든 출력이: Softmax divides each output's exponential (e^value) by the total, so every output is between 0 and 1 and they add up to 1. That's why the outputs are read as "the probability of each kind." It's almost always used in the last layer of multi-way classification, like classifying photos or choosing the next word. The name "softmax" was given by Bridle (1990). That paper also calls the same function the "normalised exponential."
Being right and how sure you are are different things.
사람도 맞혔지만 자신 없을 때가 있고, 틀렸는데 확신할 때도 있다. 자기: People also sometimes get it right but feel unsure, or get it wrong but feel certain. Knowing how much to trust your own judgment (metacognition) develops separately too.
같은 경계라도 가중치를 키우면 확률이 0이나 1 쪽으로 쏠린다. 확신은: Even with the same boundary, bigger weights push the probabilities toward 0 or 1. Higher confidence isn't better in itself; it's good when it matches the actual chance of being right (calibration). Today's large neural networks are known to be overconfident even when wrong. Guo and colleagues (2017) called this problem "calibration" and proposed "temperature scaling," which divides the outputs by a temperature to correct the probabilities. Hinton and colleagues (2015) also put a "temperature" into softmax to soften the probabilities.
시각 피질의 깊은 곳에는 얼굴, 장소, 몸 같은 범주에 따로 반응하는 영: Deep in the visual cortex there are areas that respond separately to categories like faces, places and bodies.
Keep one output neuron per kind and answer with the kind of the biggest output. If the outputs connect straight to the inputs with no hidden neurons, each kind's region becomes a convex shape surrounded by straight lines. Ten kinds of handwritten digits and 1000 kinds of photos work the same way. LeCun and colleagues' (1998) LeNet-5 had one output unit for each of the ten handwritten digits.
How surprised was it by the answer?
Many studies find that the brain learns more when its expectation misses badly (when it's surprised). The prediction error becomes the learning signal.
교차 엔트로피는 -log(정답의 확률)이다. 정답 확률이 1이면 0, 작: Cross-entropy is -log(probability of the correct answer). If the correct probability is 1 it's 0, and the smaller it is, the harder it punishes. Used with softmax, the amount to fix is a simple "probability - answer," so almost all classification networks learn with this error. It's a concept rooted in Shannon's information theory (entropy). Shannon (1948) defined the amount of information and "entropy." Cross-entropy was built later on top of this entropy.
A door that opens and closes with a single multiplication.
뇌에는 다른 뉴런의 신호가 통할지 말지를 조절하는 회로가 있다. 시상(t: The brain has circuits that control whether other neurons' signals get through. The thalamus acts as a gateway that filters whether sensory information is sent on to the cerebrum.
게이트는 0~1 사이의 값을 곱해서 신호를 통과시키거나(1) 막는다(0): A gate multiplies by a value between 0 and 1 to let a signal through (1) or block it (0). Recurrent networks like LSTM and GRU learn on their own, with these gates, what to remember and what to output. Hochreiter and Schmidhuber (1997) called these gates "multiplicative gate units."
하루에 보고 듣는 것 중 아주 일부만 기억에 남는다. 주의를 기울인 것,: Only a tiny part of what we see and hear in a day stays in memory. Only what we paid attention to, or felt was important, gets stored.
입력 게이트는 새 값을 셀에 얼마나 담을지 정한다. 문이 닫혀 있으면 새: The input gate decides how much of a new value to put in the cell. When the gate is closed the cell stays the same even if new input comes in, so it can pick out the value of the moment it needs and hold it for a long time. Hochreiter and Schmidhuber's (1997) first LSTM started with two gates, an "input gate" and an "output gate."
Forgetting well is part of remembering well.
잊는 것도 뇌의 중요한 기능이다. 쓸모없어진 기억을 지워야 새로운 것을: Forgetting is an important brain function too. Erasing memories that are no longer useful lets you learn new things without getting confused.
망각 게이트는 지난 셀 값에 곱해서 얼마나 남길지 정한다. 1997년의: The forget gate multiplies the last cell value to decide how much to keep. The first LSTM in 1997 didn't have it; it was added in 2000 to solve the problem of cell values piling up without end (Gers and colleagues). Today "LSTM" usually means the form that has it. The paper's title is literally "learning to forget." This gate's name is the "forget gate."
A memory cell with three gates.
작업 기억은 필요한 것을 붙잡아 두고, 방해 자극은 막고, 필요할 때 꺼: Working memory holds on to what's needed, blocks distractions, and takes things out when needed. There's a theory that the prefrontal cortex and basal ganglia are involved in this kind of "gate opening and closing."
LSTM 한 칸은 셀(기억)과 입력·망각·출력 게이트로 이루어진다. 게이: One LSTM cell is made of a cell (memory) and input, forget and output gates. The gate values usually come from a sigmoid between 0 and 1, and learning decides what to store, erase and take out. Until the Transformer came along, it was at the center of translation and speech recognition. Greff and colleagues (2017) removed LSTM's parts one by one and showed that the "forget gate" and the output activation function matter most. Cho and colleagues (2014) introduced a new hidden unit that cut the gates down to two, a "reset gate" and an "update gate," which later got the name GRU.
