AI의 문제점과 해결책. 정확도만 보면 속는 불균형 데이터(재현율), 배: AI's problems and their fixes. Imbalanced data that fools you if you only look at accuracy (recall), biased data that teaches shortcuts like the background, adversarial examples fooled by slightly pushed inputs (boundaries with margin), and the symmetry problem where starting the same means never learning (initialization). Overfitting and its fixes are covered in Chapter 6, "Understand, Don't Memorize."
Dots are neurons, lines are synapses.
뇌는 약 860억 개의 뉴런으로 이루어져 있다. 뉴런은 다른 뉴런에게서: The brain is made of about 86 billion neurons. A neuron receives signals from other neurons, and when enough have gathered, it sends a signal on to the next neuron. The place where one neuron meets another is a synapse.
인공 뉴런도 똑같이 생각한다. 여러 입력을 받아 계산하고 값 하나를 내보: Artificial neurons work on the same idea. They take several inputs, calculate, and send out one value. AI is a net (neural network) of thousands to billions of these neurons connected together. McCulloch and Pitts (1943) treated the neuron as an "all-or-none" element with just on and off, and wrote the activity of neural nets as logic formulas (a "logical calculus").
뉴런과 뉴런이 만나는 시냅스는 세기가 제각각이다. 자주 함께 쓰이는 시냅: The synapses where neurons meet each have their own strength. Synapses used together often grow stronger, and unused ones grow weaker (synaptic plasticity). When we learn something, synapse strengths in the brain change.
인공 뉴런은 입력 x에 가중치 w를 곱해서 받는다. 가중치가 크면 그 입: An artificial neuron receives input x multiplied by a weight w. A big weight treats that input as important, 0 ignores it, and a negative weight takes it the opposite way. When AI "learns," it's ultimately fixing these weights. Rosenblatt (1958) saw the perceptron as storing experience in the strengths of its connections and called this "information storage."
Add up all the incoming signals.
실제 뉴런 하나에는 수천 개의 시냅스가 붙어 있다. 각 시냅스에서 들어온: A single real neuron has thousands of synapses attached. The small electrical changes coming in through each synapse add up in the cell body, and if the total is big enough, the neuron fires.
인공 뉴런의 계산은 w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + … 처럼 입력마다 가중치를: An artificial neuron's calculation multiplies each input by its weight and adds them up, as in w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + …. This is called the weighted sum. Even huge language models repeat this calculation billions of times. McCulloch and Pitts's (1943) neuron turns on when incoming excitation gets over a "threshold." Today's weighted sum adds a different strength (weight) for each synapse on top of that.
How much has to gather to turn it on?
뉴런은 막전위가 문턱(역치, 대략 -55mV 근처)을 넘어야 활동 전위를: A neuron fires an action potential only when its membrane potential gets over a threshold (roughly -55 mV). Fall a little short of the threshold and nothing happens. That's why signals have to "gather" for it to respond.
퍼셉트론(1958년 로젠블랫)은 가중합이 문턱을 넘으면 1, 아니면 0을: The perceptron (Rosenblatt, 1958) outputs 1 if the weighted sum gets over the threshold, otherwise 0. The value that moves the threshold is the bias b. Think of it as the weight on an input that's always 1, and the bias is just one more weight. Rosenblatt (1958) and McCulloch and Pitts (1943) both called this value the "threshold."
Turning on actually turns it off.
억제성 시냅스는 받는 뉴런을 발화에서 멀어지게 한다. 흥분과 억제가 함께: An inhibitory synapse pushes the receiving neuron away from firing. Because excitation and inhibition exist together, the brain can compute things like "if this turns on, turn that off."
가중치가 음수면 입력이 켜질수록 출력이 작아진다. 편향(+)과 음수 가중: With a negative weight, the more the input turns on, the smaller the output gets. A bias (+) and one negative weight (-) make a NOT gate. With just AND, OR and NOT you can build any logic circuit. Eccles and colleagues (1954) confirmed in the spinal cord a synapse that switches off the receiving neuron and called it an "inhibitory synapse."
One straight line can't split it.
뇌는 뉴런 하나가 아니라 여러 층의 회로로 계산한다. 감각 정보는 여러: The brain computes not with one neuron but with circuits of many layers. Sensory information passes through many stages and turns into increasingly complex features (lines → shapes → faces).
1969년 민스키와 패퍼트는 층이 하나인 퍼셉트론이 XOR을 못 푼다는: In 1969 Minsky and Papert showed that a single-layer perceptron can't solve XOR, because the four cells can't be split by one straight line. A multilayer perceptron with a hidden layer can solve XOR. Today's deep learning stacks these layers very deep. Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams (1986) called the middle neurons that are neither input nor output "hidden units," and showed that these units make problems like XOR solvable.
Fix it by as much as it was wrong.
In 1949 Hebb proposed that "neurons that fire together wire together." Experience changes synapse strengths, and the changed synapses change the next behavior. This is thought to be the basic way the brain learns.
델타 규칙: 가중치 변화 = 학습률 × (목표 - 출력) × 입력. 틀린: The delta rule: weight change = learning rate × (target - output) × input. It fixes by as much as it was wrong, and by as much as that input was on. When it's right the error is 0, so it doesn't fix any more. Going once through all the data is called an epoch. Widrow and Lehr (1990) call this delta rule the "LMS (least mean square)" algorithm.
How much to fix at once?
뇌에서는 도파민 같은 신경 조절 물질이 \"이번 경험에서 얼마나 크게 배: In the brain, neuromodulators like dopamine are known to control "how strongly to learn from this experience." When something better than expected happens, dopamine rises and that experience is learned more strongly.
학습률이 너무 작으면 배우는 데 한참 걸리고, 너무 크면 정답을 계속 지: If the learning rate is too small, learning takes ages; too big and it keeps overshooting the answer and fails to learn at all. When training real AI, the learning rate is the first value people tune. Robbins and Monro (1951) set out the method of approaching an answer by fixing a little at a time as "stochastic approximation," and the Adam paper (Kingma and Ba 2014) calls the learning rate the "stepsize α."
Something no amount of learning can do.
재미있게도 실제 사람 대뇌 겉질 뉴런은 수상돌기에서 복잡한 계산을 해서: Interestingly, a study (2020) found that real human cortical neurons do complex calculations in their dendrites, so a single neuron can do something like XOR. Real neurons are far more complex than artificial ones.
층이 하나인 뉴런은 학습률을 어떻게 바꿔도 XOR을 배우지 못한다. 만들: A single-layer neuron can't learn XOR no matter how you change the learning rate. What can't be built can't be learned either. When this limit became known, neural network research cooled for a while in the 1970s. Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams (1986) showed that adding "hidden units" and sending the error backward gets past this limit.
뇌가 역전파를 그대로 쓰는지는 아직 논쟁 중이다. 오차 신호를 거꾸로 정: Whether the brain uses backpropagation as is remains debated, because no clear pathway has been found in the brain that sends error signals backward precisely. How the brain does something similar is still an active research topic.
출력의 오차를 그 출력에 이어진 히든 뉴런에게 가중치만큼 나눠 주고, 히: The output's error is handed back to the hidden neurons connected to it, in proportion to the weights, and the hidden neurons fix their own weights too. Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams made it widely known in 1986, and almost every neural network today learns this way. Just as the paper's title says, it learns representations "by back-propagating errors."
Learning from points instead of answers.
동물은 정답을 듣고 배우지 않는다. 먹이를 찾으면 좋고 다치면 나쁘다는: Animals don't learn by being told the answer. They change their behavior from results alone: finding food is good, getting hurt is bad. In the brain, dopamine neurons are known to guide learning by sending a signal that "it was better/worse than expected" (reward prediction error).
강화학습은 에이전트(배우는 쪽)가 환경 속에서 행동하고, 그 결과로 받은: In reinforcement learning, an agent (the learner) acts in an environment and changes its policy (rule for acting) so the sum of rewards (points) it gets grows. Unlike supervised learning, there's no answer table. The Go AI AlphaGo, walking robots and game AIs learned this way. Sutton and Barto (2018) call the learner the "agent," the rule for acting the "policy," and the points the "reward signal." Schultz and colleagues (1997) explained the dopamine signal as a reward "prediction error." The creatures in Chapter 5 learn with "evolution strategies" (Salimans and colleagues 2017), picking the highest-scoring of several candidates made by jiggling the brain slightly.
Praise that's too rare teaches nothing.
동물 훈련사는 최종 동작을 바로 기다리지 않는다. 목표에 조금씩 가까워질: Animal trainers don't just wait for the final move. They guide the animal by praising it each time it gets a little closer to the goal (shaping). It's the method Skinner used in his pigeon experiments.
보상이 아주 드물면(희소 보상) 에이전트는 우연히 성공하기 전까지 어떤: When rewards are very rare (sparse rewards), the agent can't tell which direction is good until it succeeds by chance. Giving small rewards at the steps along the way is called reward shaping. But give the in-between rewards wrongly and it can learn something odd, as in the next experiment. Skinner (1958) called this method of rewarding each step closer to the target behavior "shaping."
You have to use points to say what to avoid, too.
아픔과 두려움도 학습 신호다. 뜨거운 것에 한 번 데면 다시는 만지지 않: Pain and fear are learning signals too. Get burned by something hot once and you never want to touch it again. In the brain, areas like the amygdala leave strong memories tied to danger.
보상은 음수가 될 수도 있다. 에이전트는 \"점수의 합\"만 보기 때문에: Rewards can be negative too. Since the agent only looks at "the sum of points," to make it avoid dangerous actions you have to give those actions a penalty. In safety-critical fields like self-driving cars, deciding what gets how big a penalty matters enormously. Thorndike (1898) showed with cats in puzzle boxes that actions followed by good results increase and actions followed by bad results decrease. This principle later (1905) got the name "law of effect."
AI learns what you gave points for, not what you wanted.
사람도 비슷하다. 시험 점수만 보상하면 이해하지 않고 외우는 쪽으로, 조: People are similar. Reward only test scores and behavior shifts toward memorizing without understanding; reward only view counts and it shifts toward the sensational. There's a saying that when a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure (Goodhart's law).
2016년 한 보트 경주 게임에서, 경로의 아이템을 먹으면 점수를 주자: In a 2016 boat-racing game, when points were given for picking up items along the course, the AI circled the same spot picking up items instead of heading for the finish line. Finding gaps in the reward like this is called reward hacking, and it's a core problem in research on making AI follow people's real intentions (alignment). "Reward hacking" is one of the AI safety problems laid out by Amodei and colleagues (2016).
Stick to the known path, or try a new one?
어린 동물은 많이 돌아다니며 탐험하고, 자라면서 아는 방법을 더 많이 쓴: Young animals roam a lot and explore, and as they grow they use the methods they know more. The brain constantly weighs a sure reward against new possibilities.
가장 좋다고 아는 행동만 하면(활용) 더 좋은 것을 영영 못 찾고, 새: If you only do what you know is best (exploitation), you never find anything better; if you only try new things (exploration), you can't enjoy the good things you know. This is called the exploration-exploitation dilemma. ε-greedy is the simplest fix: with probability ε try any action, and otherwise pick the action with the best Q. Often ε starts big and shrinks as learning goes on. Auer and colleagues (2002) called this problem, which reinforcement learning always faces, the "exploration versus exploitation dilemma," and compared ε-greedy with UCB.
신호를 받아 계산하고 값 하나를 다음으로 보내는 단위. 이 게임의 동그라: A unit that receives signals, calculates, and passes one value on. The circles in this game.
뉴런과 뉴런을 잇는 연결. 이 게임의 선. 신호를 얼마나 세게 전할지(가: A connection between two neurons. The lines in this game. It carries how strongly to pass the signal on (the weight).
시냅스의 세기. 클수록 세게, 0이면 무시, 음수면 반대로 전한다. AI: The strength of a synapse. Bigger passes it on more strongly, 0 ignores it, negative passes it on reversed. When AI learns, it's fixing these values.
All the incoming values × weights added up. The first step of a neuron's calculation.
입력과 상관없이 늘 더해지는 값. 이 게임에서는 언제나 1인 \"상시\": A value that's always added, regardless of input. In this game, the weight on the "always-on" neuron, which is always 1. It moves the threshold for turning on.
가중합을 어떤 값으로 내보낼지 정하는 함수. 0~1 자르기, ReLU,: The function that decides what value to send out from the weighted sum. Clip to 0–1, ReLU, sigmoid, step and more. From the "Creature Navigation" chapter on, you can change it by clicking a neuron.
0보다 작으면 0, 크면 그대로 내보내는 함수. 계산이 빠르고 잘 배워서: A function that outputs 0 for values below 0 and passes larger values through as is. It's fast to compute and learns well, so it's the most used in today's neural networks.
어떤 값이든 0과 1 사이의 S자 곡선으로 바꾸는 함수. 확률처럼 읽고: A function that turns any value into an S-shaped curve between 0 and 1. Used when you want to read the output like a probability.
같은 단계에 있는 뉴런 묶음. 입력층 → 히든층 → 출력층 순서로 신호가: A group of neurons at the same stage. Signals flow in order: input layer → hidden layer → output layer. A network with many layers is a "deep" neural network (deep learning).
입력층과 출력층 사이(히든층)에 있는 뉴런. 밖에서는 값이 보이지 않고,: A neuron between the input and output layers (in the hidden layer). Its value can't be seen from outside, and it handles in-between calculations. Thanks to it, the network can make judgments one straight line can't (XOR and so on).
가중합이 문턱을 넘으면 1, 아니면 0을 내는 가장 단순한 인공 뉴런(1: The simplest artificial neuron, outputting 1 if the weighted sum gets over the threshold and 0 otherwise (Rosenblatt, 1958). Stack several layers and you get a multilayer perceptron.
0과 1을 받아 0과 1을 내는 규칙. AND(둘 다 1), OR(하나라: Rules that take 0s and 1s and output 0 or 1. AND (both 1), OR (either 1), NOT (the opposite), XOR (exactly one 1). You build them yourself with neurons in the "One Neuron" and "Logic Circuit Puzzles" chapters.
틀린 만큼 가중치를 고쳐서 점점 맞게 만드는 과정. 데이터를 한 바퀴 다: The process of fixing the weights by as much as they were wrong so they gradually get it right. Going once through all the data is called an epoch (one round of learning).
The difference between the target and the output. Learning fixes the weights in the direction that shrinks this value.
한 번에 가중치를 얼마나 크게 고칠지. 너무 작으면 느리고, 너무 크면: How much to change the weights at once. Too small is slow; too big overshoots the answer and fails to learn.
입력을 정해진 몇 가지 종류 중 하나로 나누는 일. \"이 사진은 고양이: Sorting inputs into one of a fixed set of kinds. Like "this photo is a cat" or "this email is spam." In Chapter 6 you sort points into blue and orange.
분류의 답이 바뀌는 경계선. 뉴런 하나의 결정 경계는 직선이고, 히든 뉴: The boundary line where a classifier's answer changes. A single neuron's decision boundary is straight; with hidden neurons it can bend or close into a shape.
AI가 배우는 데 쓰는 데이터와, 배운 뒤 실력을 재는 처음 보는 데이터: The data an AI learns from, and new data it has never seen that measures its skill after learning. You only know its real skill when you measure on test data.
훈련 데이터의 잡음까지 외워서, 훈련 데이터는 잘 맞히지만 처음 보는 데: Memorizing even the noise in the training data, so it does well on the training data but gets new data wrong.
배운 것을 처음 보는 데이터에도 잘 적용하는 능력. AI를 만드는 진짜: The ability to apply what was learned to data never seen before. The real goal of building AI.
오차가 줄어드는 방향으로 가중치를 조금씩 옮기는 학습 방법. 학습률은 한: A learning method that moves the weights little by little in the direction that shrinks the error. The learning rate is the size of one step.
작은 필터를 그림 위에서 한 칸씩 옮기며, 겹친 칸끼리 곱해서 더하는 계: A calculation that moves a small filter across a picture one cell at a time, multiplying overlapping cells and adding them up. The same filter is used at every spot (weight sharing).
합성곱에 쓰는 작은 가중치 격자(예: 3×3). 필터 모양에 따라 세로줄: A small grid of weights used in convolution (e.g. 3×3). Depending on its shape, a filter finds different features like vertical lines, horizontal lines and edges.
필터 하나를 그림 전체에 적용한 결과. 그 특징이 그림의 어디에 있는지: The result of applying one filter across the whole picture. It shows where in the picture that feature is.
특징 맵을 줄이는 계산. 최대 풀링은 가장 큰 값만 남겨 \"이 특징이: A calculation that shrinks a feature map. Max pooling keeps only the biggest value and passes on "this feature was somewhere."
합성곱 → 풀링을 여러 번 쌓고 마지막에 분류하는 신경망. 사진·영상 인: A neural network that stacks convolution → pooling several times and classifies at the end. The basic structure of photo and video recognition.
뉴런의 값을 다음 순간의 입력으로 되돌려 보내는 신경망. 시간 순서가 있: A neural network that sends neurons' values back as input at the next moment. It handles data with a time order. In Chapter 8 you build one with memory neurons.
RNN이 지금까지 본 입력을 요약해 들고 다니는 값. 이 게임에서는 기억: The value an RNN carries around that summarizes the input it has seen so far. In this game, it's the value of the hidden neurons that comes back through the memory neurons.
순서가 있는 데이터. 문장, 소리, 날마다의 기온처럼 앞뒤 순서에 뜻이: Data with an order. Like sentences, sounds or daily temperatures, the order carries meaning.
기억을 남길지 지울지 정하는 문(게이트)을 단 RNN. 기본 RNN보다: An RNN with gates that decide whether to keep or erase memory. It remembers much further into the past than a basic RNN.
정답(꼬리표) 없이 데이터 속 구조를 찾는 학습. 군집화와 오토인코더가: Learning that finds structure in data without answers (labels). Clustering and autoencoders are the classic examples.
Grouping similar data into clusters. In Chapter 9 you group points.
중심 k개를 두고 \"가장 가까운 중심에 묶기 → 중심을 평균으로 옮기기: A clustering method that keeps k centers and repeats "group with the nearest center → move each center to the average" until it stops.
주변보다는 낮지만 가장 낮지는 않은 골짜기. 학습이 여기에 갇히면 더 좋: A valley lower than its surroundings but not the lowest of all. If learning gets trapped here, it can't find a better answer.
입력을 작은 코드로 줄였다가(인코더) 다시 살리는(디코더) 신경망. 입력: A neural network that shrinks the input into a small code (encoder) and brings it back (decoder). It learns with the input itself as the target.
오토인코더의 코드 값들이 놓이는 공간. 잘 배우면 비슷한 입력이 가까운: The space where an autoencoder's code values sit. When it learns well, similar inputs end up in nearby places.

가중치마다 기울기의 평균과 크기를 기억해서 걸음 크기를 따로 맞추는 최적: An optimization method that remembers each weight's average gradient and gradient size and sets each step size separately. The most used today.

지금 가치 = 한 걸음 보상 + γ × 다음 상태의 가치. 가치를 상태에: Value now = reward for one step + γ × value of the next state. The equation that links value from state to state.
한 걸음 늦게 받는 보상에 곱하는 0~1 사이의 수. 작으면 눈앞의 보상: A number between 0 and 1 you multiply a reward by for each step it comes later. Small means looking at the reward right in front; big means looking at distant rewards too.
상태마다 행동별 점수 Q를 두고, 직접 해 보며 \"보상 + γ × 다음: A reinforcement learning method that keeps a score Q for each action in each state and, by actually trying things, keeps fixing it toward "reward + γ × the best Q of the next state."
ε의 확률로는 아무 행동이나 해 보고(탐험), 나머지는 가장 좋다고 아는: A method that tries any action with probability ε (exploration) and otherwise does the action it knows is best (exploitation).

LSTM이 칸에서 칸으로 넘기는 기억 값. 게이트들이 무엇을 담고 지우고: The memory value an LSTM passes from cell to cell. The gates decide what to store, erase and take out.

The side that acts and learns in reinforcement learning. In this game it's the creature "Dot." The world the agent acts in (the arena) is called the environment.
행동의 결과로 받는 점수. 좋은 일에는 +, 피해야 할 일에는 -. 사람: Points received as the result of an action. + for good things, - for things to avoid. A person deciding what gets how many points is called reward design.
어떤 상황에서 어떻게 행동할지 정하는 규칙. 이 게임에서는 감각을 바퀴에: The rule that decides how to act in each situation. In this game, the weights connecting senses to wheels are the policy.
새로운 행동을 시도해 볼지(탐험), 지금까지 좋았던 행동을 계속할지(활용: Weighing whether to try new actions (exploration) or keep doing actions that have worked so far (exploitation).
AI가 사람이 원한 목표 대신 점수 규칙의 빈틈을 찾아 점수만 올리는 것: When AI finds gaps in the scoring rules and just pumps up its score instead of the goal people wanted. It happens when "what you gave points for" and "what you want" differ.
출력의 오차를 앞쪽 뉴런들에게 거꾸로 나눠 주며 모든 가중치를 고치는 방: A method that hands the output's error back to earlier neurons and fixes every weight. Almost every neural network learns this way.
한쪽 종류가 아주 적은 데이터. 모두 많은 쪽이라고만 답해도 정확도가 높: Data where one kind is very rare. Answering the common kind for everything still gives high accuracy, so accuracy alone can't show how good a model is.
진짜 그 종류인 것 중에서 AI가 찾아낸 비율. 병 찾기처럼 놓치면 안: Of the things that really are that kind, the share the AI found. Important for tasks where missing one is not OK, like detecting a disease.
AI가 그 종류라고 답한 것 중에서 진짜로 맞은 비율. 재현율과 함께 본: Of the things the AI said were that kind, the share that really were. Looked at together with recall.
배경처럼 훈련 데이터에서만 우연히 통하는 단서를 배우는 것. 처음 보는: Learning clues, like the background, that only happen to work in the training data. It gets new data wrong.
결정 경계와 가장 가까운 데이터 사이의 거리. 클수록 입력이 조금 바뀌어: The distance between the decision boundary and the nearest data point. The bigger it is, the less the answer changes when the input shifts a little.
학습을 시작할 때의 가중치를 정하는 일. 모두 같은 값이면 뉴런들이 똑같: Deciding the weights at the start of learning. If they're all the same value, the neurons learn the same thing, so they start at small random values.
검증 데이터의 오차가 다시 커지기 시작하면 학습을 멈추는 방법. 과적합을: A method that stops learning when the error on validation data starts to grow again. It prevents overfitting.
뉴런을 켜짐·꺼짐 두 가지만 내는 논리 소자로 본 최초의 인공 뉴런 모델: The first artificial neuron model, treating the neuron as a logic element that outputs only on or off.
The paper that first proposed the perceptron, which learns by fixing its own weights.
역전파로 히든 유닛이 스스로 쓸모 있는 표현을 배운다는 것을 보였다. X: Showed that with backpropagation, hidden units learn useful representations on their own. It solves problems like XOR.
논리식(AND·OR·NOT)을 스위치 회로로 바꾸는 법. 디지털 회로 설: How to turn logic formulas (AND, OR, NOT) into switching circuits. The starting point of digital circuit design.
연산 하나만으로 모든 논리를 나타낼 수 있음을 보였다. 셰퍼는 NOR(둘: Showed that all of logic can be expressed with a single operation. Sheffer showed it with NOR (neither), and NAND, which has the same property, was first used by Nicod in 1917.
시각 피질 뉴런이 특정 방향의 선에만 반응한다는 발견. 합성곱 필터의 뿌: The discovery that visual cortex neurons respond only to lines at a particular angle. The root of convolution filters.
The layered structure of visual processing, from simple cells to complex cells.
The prototype of the CNN, alternating layers of filters and layers that gather.
Read handwritten zip codes by having convolution filters learned with backpropagation.
합성곱 → 풀링 → 분류로 이어지는 LeNet-5. CNN의 교과서 같은: LeNet-5, running convolution → pooling → classification. Something like the textbook paper on CNNs.
깊은 CNN으로 사진 1000가지 분류에서 크게 이기며 딥러닝 붐을 연: AlexNet, which won big at classifying photos into 1000 kinds with a deep CNN and kicked off the deep learning boom. The link is the version republished in a journal in 2017.
개구리 눈의 뉴런이 이미 '움직이는 작은 점' 같은 특징을 골라 보낸다는: The discovery that neurons in the frog's eye already pick out and send features like "a small moving dot."
A computational theory of finding where brightness changes (edges). The classic on edge filters.
Measured lateral inhibition, where neighboring neurons suppress each other, in the horseshoe crab's eye.
Confirmed in the spinal cord the inhibitory synapse that switches off the next neuron.
The simple recurrent network (Elman network) that feeds hidden values back as input at the next moment. It also handles XOR in time.
기억을 남길지 지울지 정하는 문(게이트)으로 긴 기억 문제를 푼 LSTM: LSTM, which solved the long-memory problem with gates that decide whether to keep or erase memory.
Showed why a basic RNN struggles to learn the distant past (the vanishing gradient).
되먹임으로 이어진 뉴런들이 안정된 상태에 머무르며 기억을 담는 호프필드: The Hopfield network, where neurons connected by feedback settle into stable states and hold memories.
자극이 사라진 뒤에도 계속 발화하며 정보를 붙잡는 뉴런을 원숭이 뇌에서: Found neurons in the monkey brain that keep firing after the stimulus is gone, holding on to information.

k-means++, which picks starting spots carefully to reduce getting trapped in wrong answers.
The start of the "elbow" method, changing the number of clusters and looking for where the scatter bends.
가장 잘 맞는 뉴런만 이겨서 배우는 경쟁 학습으로 정답 없이 특징을 찾는: Finds features without answers through competitive learning, where only the best-matching neuron wins and learns.
The self-organizing map, which arranges itself so similar inputs gather on neighboring neurons.
The paper that shrank data into a small code with a deep autoencoder and restored it.
The denoising autoencoder, which learns to restore the original from noisy input.
The variational autoencoder (VAE), which samples new data from the latent space and draws it.
잡음을 조금씩 걷어 내며 그림을 그리는 확산 모델. 그림 생성 AI의 바: The diffusion model, which draws pictures by stripping away noise little by little. The basis of image-generating AI.
word2vec, which turns words into meaningful bundles of numbers (embeddings).
A review of how to learn good representations on one's own.
The discovery of place cells, which fire only when a rat is at a particular spot.
The discovery of grid cells, which represent space with a grid-shaped code.
The textbook of reinforcement learning. The authors made the full text freely available.
도파민 뉴런이 '예상보다 좋았나'를 신호로 보낸다는 발견. 뇌의 보상 학: The discovery that dopamine neurons signal "was it better than expected?" Reward learning in the brain.
DQN, which learned Atari games at human level from just the screen and the score.
가중치를 조금씩 흔든 후보 중 점수가 높은 쪽으로 가는 진화 전략. 5장: Evolution strategies, which move toward the highest-scoring of several candidates made by jiggling the weights slightly. The same idea as how Chapter 5 learns.
Laid out problems like reward hacking, where an AI pumps up its score against the intent.
목표 행동에 조금씩 다가갈 때마다 보상하는 '조형(shaping)'을 소: Introduced "shaping," rewarding each step closer to the target behavior.
상자 속 고양이 실험으로, 결과가 좋은 행동은 늘고 나쁜 행동은 줄어든다: Showed with cats in puzzle boxes that actions with good results increase and actions with bad results decrease. The principle got the name "law of effect" in 1905. The starting point of learning from rewards and penalties.
사람 눈에 안 보이는 작은 변화로 신경망을 속이는 적대적 예제를 처음 보: First reported adversarial examples, which fool neural networks with tiny changes invisible to the human eye.
Explained why adversarial examples happen and proposed a way to defend against them.
히든 층 하나에 뉴런이 충분하면 어떤 모양의 함수도 흉내 낼 수 있다(보: With enough neurons in a single hidden layer, a network can imitate a function of any shape (universal approximation).
Another classic showing that multilayer networks are universal approximators.
Linear discriminant analysis, which separated iris species with a straight line made by weighting and adding measurements.
신경망은 무작위 꼬리표까지 외울 수 있다. 외우기와 일반화의 차이를 다시: Neural networks can memorize even random labels. It asks again what separates memorizing from generalizing.
Dropout, which reduces overfitting by switching neurons off at random during training.
조금씩 고쳐 가며 답에 다가가는 확률적 근사. 경사 하강법과 학습률의 수: Stochastic approximation, approaching an answer by fixing a little at a time. The mathematical root of gradient descent and the learning rate.
가중치마다 걸음 크기(학습률)를 알아서 맞추는 Adam. 지금 가장 널리: Adam, which sets the step size (learning rate) for each weight automatically. The most widely used today.
델타 규칙(LMS)을 만든 위드로가 퍼셉트론부터 역전파까지 학습 규칙을: Widrow, who created the delta rule (LMS), surveys learning rules from the perceptron to backpropagation.
The first connectome, drawing every connection of the 302 neurons of the roundworm C. elegans.
Central pattern generator circuits that make walking and swimming rhythms without commands from the brain.
빙글빙글 도는 빛 센서 하나와 바퀴로 빛을 찾아가는 로봇 거북. 이 게임: A robot tortoise that seeks light with one spinning light sensor and wheels. The grandparent of this game's creatures.
Explained the sea slug's gill-withdrawal reflex at the level of a few neurons.
쥐 수염 하나하나가 대뇌 피질의 '통(barrel)' 하나씩에 대응하는: A touch map where each rat whisker matches one "barrel" in the cortex.
실제 신경망의 오차 지형을 그려서, 바닥이 넓고 평평할수록 처음 보는 데: Drew the error landscapes of real neural networks and showed that the wider and flatter the bottom, the better they do on unseen data (generalization).
시작점에서 끝점까지 직선을 따라 오차를 재 보며 학습이 지나는 지형을 살: Studied the landscape learning passes through by measuring the error along a straight line from start to end.
지난 걸음의 방향을 더해 빨리 내려가는 '무거운 공(heavy ball): The "heavy ball" method, which adds the direction of the last step to go downhill faster. The origin of momentum.
모멘텀과 좋은 시작값만으로도 깊은 신경망을 잘 학습시킬 수 있음을 보였다: Showed that momentum and good starting values alone can train deep neural networks well.
차원이 아주 많으면 웅덩이보다 안장점이 학습을 더 많이 늦춘다는 것을 밝: Showed that with very many dimensions, saddle points slow learning more than puddles do.
가중치마다 지금까지의 기울기 크기로 걸음을 나누는 AdaGrad. Ada: AdaGrad, which divides each weight's step by the size of its gradients so far. The basis of Adam.
큰 문제를 '지금 한 걸음 + 남은 문제'로 쪼개는 동적 계획법. 벨만: Dynamic programming, splitting a big problem into "one step now + the rest of the problem." The starting point of the Bellman equation.
미래의 만족을 일정한 비율로 깎아 더하는 할인 효용 모델. 할인율 γ의: The discounted utility model, shaving future satisfaction by a fixed rate and adding it up. The economics root of the discount γ.
Proved that with enough exploration, Q-learning converges to the best action scores.
A classic on the math of which slot machine to pull (exploration and exploitation). It compares ε-greedy and UCB.
The paper that set out the name "softmax" and how it lets outputs be read as probabilities.
요즘 신경망은 틀릴 때도 지나치게 확신한다는 것을 보이고, 온도로 확률을: Showed that today's neural networks are overconfident even when wrong, and proposed correcting the probabilities with a temperature.
소프트맥스에 온도를 넣어 확률을 부드럽게 만들고, 큰 모델의 지식을 작은: Puts a temperature into softmax to soften the probabilities and transfers a big model's knowledge into a small one.
정보의 양과 엔트로피를 정의한 정보 이론의 출발점. 교차 엔트로피는 이: The starting point of information theory, defining the amount of information and entropy. Cross-entropy is a concept built later on top of this entropy.
LSTM에 망각 게이트를 더해, 쌓이기만 하던 셀 기억을 스스로 지울 수: Added a forget gate to LSTM so the cell memory, which used to only pile up, can erase itself.
LSTM의 게이트를 하나씩 빼 보며 어떤 부품이 중요한지 대규모로 비교했: Removed LSTM's gates one by one to compare at scale which parts matter. The forget gate and the output side are key.
리셋 게이트·업데이트 게이트 두 개로 LSTM을 단순하게 만든 새 히든: Introduced a new hidden unit that simplifies LSTM to two gates, reset and update. It later got the name GRU.
한쪽 종류가 아주 적은 데이터에서 생기는 문제와 재표집·비용 조정 같은: A review of the problems that arise in data where one kind is very rare, and fixes like resampling and cost adjustment.
훈련 데이터에서만 통하는 지름길을 배우는 문제를 \"지름길 학습(shor: Gave the name "shortcut learning" to the problem of learning shortcuts that only work on the training data.

The support vector machine, which picks the boundary with the largest gap (margin) between two groups.
Adversarial training, which makes networks robust by training on deliberately pushed adversarial examples.
시작 가중치의 크기가 깊은 신경망 학습을 좌우한다는 것을 보이고, 층 크: Showed that the size of the starting weights decides how deep networks train, and proposed an initialization matched to layer size.

과적합을 막는 방법도 여럿 있다. 검증 데이터의 오차가 다시 커지기 시작: There are also several ways to prevent overfitting. Synapse Arena is a place to learn AI from the basics by wiring neurons yourself. In this tutorial you'll try every control one at a time. You can skip any time with Esc.
여기가 뇌를 만드는 곳이에요. 동그라미 하나가 뉴런, 뉴런을 잇는 선이: This is where you build the brain. Each circle is a neuron, and the lines connecting them are synapses. Signals flow from left to right.

언제나 1인 뉴런이에요. 여기에 붙은 선의 세기가 \"편향\"이 되어,: A neuron that is always 1. The strength of a line attached to it becomes the "bias," raising or lowering the threshold for turning on.
입력과 출력 사이에서 중간 계산을 하는 뉴런이에요. 실험마다 처음부터 2: Neurons that do in-between calculations between inputs and outputs. Each experiment starts with 2, and you can drag them around. When you want to use one, just connect lines.
The brain's answer. A value of 0.5 or more reads as 1, below as 0.
입력 A 동그라미(또는 오른쪽 작은 점)를 누른 채로 끌어서, 오른쪽 \: Press and hold the input A circle (or the small dot to its right), drag it, and let go over "Output" on the right.
선(시냅스)이 생겼어요! 파란 선은 흥분(+), 빨간 선은 억제(-)예요: A line (synapse) appeared! Blue lines excite (+), red lines inhibit (-). Click the new line or the number on it to select it.
아래 막대를 왼쪽으로 끌어 세기를 0.3까지 내려 보세요. 선 위에서 마: Drag the slider below to the left to lower the strength to 0.3. Rolling the mouse wheel over a line also changes it by 0.1. "Flip sign" switches excite ↔ inhibit.
세기가 0.3이면 A가 1이어도 출력이 0.3이라 0.5를 못 넘어서 ✗: At strength 0.3, even when A is 1 the output is 0.3, which doesn't reach 0.5, so it became ✗. "Target" is the right answer for that row, and "Output" is the current brain's answer. Click the third row (A=1, B=0).
이제 뇌 편집기가 A=1, B=0일 때를 보여 줘요. 동그라미 안의 숫자: Now the brain editor shows the case A=1, B=0. The number in each circle is that neuron's current value, and the dots flowing along the lines are signals.
선을 골라 세기를 0.5 이상(예: 1)으로 올려서 진리표의 모든 줄을: Select the line and raise its strength to 0.5 or more (e.g. 1) so every row of the truth table becomes ✓.
↶ 되돌리기(Ctrl+Z), ↷ 다시 하기(Ctrl+Y), 비우기. 선: ↶ Undo (Ctrl+Z), ↷ Redo (Ctrl+Y), Clear. To delete one line, right-click it, or select it and press Delete.
Click a hidden or output neuron and an explanation and "activation function" appear below. From Chapter 3 Creature Navigation you can use functions like ReLU, sigmoid and step, and in the Lab you can even put in AND, OR, NOT, XOR gates and softmax yourself.

노란 칩이 이 실험의 목표, 옆의 칩들은 별 조건이에요. 목표를 채우면: The yellow chip is this experiment's goal, and the chips next to it are star conditions. Reach the goal for 1 star, and meet the conditions too for more stars.

생명체 길찾기 장부터는 뇌가 몸을 움직여요. 흰 동그라미가 생명체 \"도: From the Creature Navigation chapter on, the brain moves a body. The white circle is the creature "Dot," and the yellow dot is food. The orange and yellow fans are the fields of view of the left and right eyes.
On the left are the sensory neurons (eyes, feelers, whiskers, always-on), and on the right the left and right wheels. If the right wheel is faster, it turns left.
실행(Space)을 누르면 그다음부터는 뇌가 혼자 판단해요. 실행 중에: Press Run (Space) and from then on the brain decides on its own. If you edit the brain while it's running, it resets from the start.
Sends the creature back to the start (R).
\"감각 범위\"를 켜면 더듬이가 닿는 거리와 눈 값이 숫자로 보이고,: Turn on "Sensing range" to see how far the feelers reach and the eye values as numbers; "Trail" leaves marks where the creature has been.
Elapsed time and the remaining goal are shown here.
이제 히든·바퀴 뉴런을 클릭하면 ReLU, 선형, 계단, 시그모이드, t: Now when you click a hidden or wheel neuron, you can pick a function from ReLU, linear, step, sigmoid and tanh.
지금까지는 사람이 뉴런을 잇거나(1~3장), 정답 표를 보고 배웠어요(4: So far, people wired the neurons (Ch. 1–3) or it learned from an answer table (Ch. 4). Reinforcement learning has no answers. It acts, and changes itself in the direction that makes the "points (reward)" it gets grow. It's like giving a dog a treat when it does well in training.
맨 위 큰 화면이에요. 생명체 \"도트\"가 배우는 쪽(에이전트), 아레: This is the big screen at the top. The creature "Dot" is the learner (agent), and the arena is the world (environment). Right now the brain hasn't learned anything, so it stays still. While learning, the best brain found so far moves here. Scroll down with the mouse wheel to find the reward rules and the brain.
맨 아래에 있는 뇌예요. 이번에는 선을 직접 잇지 않아요. 감각 → 바퀴: This is the brain at the very bottom. This time you don't connect lines yourself. Every sense → wheel line is there, and learning decides the weights (numbers). These weights are the rules for "how to move in which situation," that is, the policy.
Decide what gets how many points. + for good things, - for things to avoid. The creature learns "what you gave points for," not what you wanted. This is reward design.
한 세대마다 뇌를 얼마나 크게 바꿔 볼지예요. 너무 작으면 새로운 행동을: How much to change the brain each generation. Too small and it can't find new behavior; too big and it breaks even what was working.
한 세대마다 지금 뇌를 조금씩 바꾼 후보 6개를 시험해 보고, 점수를 더: Each generation it tests 6 candidates made by changing the current brain a little, and keeps a candidate if it scored more (trial and error). Repeat this and the brain gradually changes. Press again during training to stop.
1×는 0.3초에 1세대씩 배워요. 2×·4×·8×로 올리면 더 빨리 배: At 1× it learns one generation every 0.3 s. Raise it to 2×, 4× or 8× to learn faster (on a slow computer the screen may stutter briefly).
세대마다 받은 최고 점수예요. 선이 올라가면 점수를 더 잘 받게 됐다는: The best score earned each generation. If the line goes up, it's getting better at earning points. But a rising score doesn't always mean it reached the real goal.
세대마다 지금 뇌로 진짜 목표(먹이 몇 개 등)를 시험해요. 목표를 이루: Each generation, the current brain is tested on the real goal (how many pieces of food, etc.). Reach the goal and the experiment is cleared. If it can't within the set number of generations, rethink the reward rules.
\"먹이를 먹으면\"에 +5를 주고, 학습 시작(또는 Space)을 눌러: Give "When it eats food" +5 and press Start training (or Space).
휠을 올려 위의 큰 화면을 보세요. 생명체가 점점 먹이 쪽으로 가는 법을: Scroll up to see the big screen above. The creature gradually figures out how to head for the food. Each time a better brain is found, it starts moving again from the beginning. When it reaches the goal, a results window pops up.
가로가 x 좌표, 세로가 y 좌표예요. 점의 색이 정답이에요(주황 = 0: Across is the x coordinate, up and down the y coordinate. A point's color is its answer (orange = 0, blue = 1). The brain has to get the color right by looking only at the point's position (x, y).
배경은 평면의 모든 자리에서 뇌에게 물어본 답이에요. 파랑 배경은 \"파: The background is the answer you get by asking the brain at every spot on the plane. Blue background is "where it answers blue," orange background "where it answers orange." The white line where the two colors meet is the decision boundary.
점의 위치가 이 두 입력 뉴런으로 들어와요. 0(왼쪽·아래) ~ 1(오른: A point's position comes in through these two input neurons. 0 (left, bottom) to 1 (right, top).
점을 누르면 그 점일 때의 뇌 값이 왼쪽 뇌 편집기에 보여요. 틀린 점은: Click a point to see the brain's values for that point in the brain editor on the left. Wrong points are marked with a red outline.
맞힌 점의 개수예요. 시험 데이터가 있는 실험에서는 채점할 때 처음 보는: The number of points it got right. In experiments with test data, grading also uses unseen points (squares).
x 좌표 뉴런을 끌어서 출력에 이어 보세요. 배경 색과 경계가 바로 바뀌: Drag the x coordinate neuron to the output to connect it. The background color and boundary change right away.
선의 세기를 바꾸면 경계가 가팔라지거나 완만해지고, 상시(편향) 선을 이: Change the line's strength and the boundary gets steeper or gentler; connect the always-on (bias) line and the boundary shifts sideways. When every point is right, check (Space).
사진 속 고양이를 알아보는 AI(CNN)는 그림 전체를 한 번에 보지 않: An AI that recognizes a cat in a photo (CNN) doesn't look at the whole picture at once. It moves a small "filter" across the picture one cell at a time, repeating the same calculation on the overlapping cells. In this chapter you paint that filter yourself.
A 6×6-cell picture. Bright cells are 1, dark cells are 0.
3×3 필터예요. 칸을 누르면 0 → +1 → -1 순서로 바뀌고, 휠로: A 3×3 filter. Click a cell to cycle 0 → +1 → -1; the wheel changes it by 0.5 and right-click sets 0. Lay the filter over a 3×3 spot of the picture and add up all the (picture cell × filter cell).
더한 값에 마지막으로 더하는 수예요. 음수로 하면 \"많이 겹칠 때만\": A number added last to the sum. Make it negative and it turns on "only when a lot overlaps."
필터를 그림의 4×4 자리에 차례로 겹쳐 계산한 결과예요. 0.5 이상이: The result of laying the filter over each 4×4 spot of the picture in turn. 0.5 or more is bright (on). Cells with a gold outline are the ones that should be on. If the lit cells match the gold outlines in every picture, you win!
Click the middle cell of the filter to make it +1. The feature map changes right away.
When it matches the target, press Check (Space). If you're stuck, look at a hint.
이번 장에서는 입력이 한 번에 하나씩, 시간 순서대로 들어와요. 뇌는 칸: In this chapter the inputs come in one at a time, in time order. The brain calculates once per cell and gives an answer for each cell.
한 줄이 한 순서예요. 왼쪽 칸부터 1, 2, 3… 차례로 입력이 들어와: Each row is one sequence. Inputs come in from the left cell, 1, 2, 3 … in turn. "Target" is the right answer for that cell and "Output" is the brain's answer. Wrong cells show in red.
기억 1에는 히든 1이 바로 전 칸에 낸 값이 들어와요. 점선 화살표가: Memory 1 receives the value hidden 1 gave in the previous cell. The dotted arrow is that feedback. In the first cell of a row there's no memory yet, so it's 0.
Click a cell to see the brain's values at that moment in the brain editor on the left.
Drag input A to hidden 1 to connect it.
기억 1 줄에 바로 전 칸의 입력이 한 칸씩 밀려 나타나요. 이제 기억: In the memory 1 row, the input from the previous cell appears shifted by one cell. Now connect memory 1 to the output and check when every cell is right (Space).
이번 장의 점에는 정답 색이 없어요. 뇌가 스스로 비슷한 점끼리 묶게 해: The points in this chapter have no answer colors. Let the brain group similar points on its own. This is called unsupervised learning.
큰 동그라미(×)가 중심이에요. 각 점은 가장 가까운 중심의 색을 받아요: The big circles (×) are centers. Each point takes the color of the nearest center. The thin lines show which center each point is grouped with.
모든 점과 자기 중심 사이 거리(제곱)를 더한 값이에요. 작을수록 잘 묶: The sum of the (squared) distances between every point and its center. The smaller it is, the better the grouping. It's the "cost" the AI tries to reduce.
중심 하나를 끌어서 다른 무리로 옮겨 보세요. 점의 색과 거리 합이 바로: Drag one center over to another cluster. The point colors and the distance sum change right away.
눈에 보이는 두 무리가 서로 다른 색이 되면 채점하세요(Space). 다: When the two visible clusters have different colors, check (Space). From the next experiment on, the computer moves the centers with the "One step" button.
이번 장의 뇌는 입력을 그대로 다시 그려 내요. 단, 가운데 작은 히든: In this chapter the brain redraws its input exactly. But it must pass through a small hidden neuron (the code) in the middle.
입력은 출력에 바로 이을 수 없어요. 모든 정보가 이 히든 뉴런을 지나가: Inputs can't connect straight to outputs. All the information must pass through this hidden neuron. Input → code is called the encoder, and code → output the decoder.
진리표와 코드: The truth table and the code
\"코드\" 칸은 그 입력일 때 히든 뉴런의 값이에요. 입력마다 코드가: The "Code" column is the hidden neuron's value for that input. The code must differ for each input so the decoder can tell them apart.
입력마다 코드 값을 점으로 찍은 지도예요(잠재 공간). 서로 다른 입력이: A map plotting each input's code values as points (the latent space). Different inputs should sit apart from each other for good compression.
입력 A를 끌어서 히든 1에 이어 보세요. 코드 지도에서 A와 B가 갈라: Drag input A to hidden 1 to connect it. A and B split apart on the code map.
이제 히든 1에서 출력 1, 2로 가는 디코더를 만들어 모든 줄이 맞으면: Now build the decoder from hidden 1 to outputs 1 and 2, and check when every row is right (Space).
가중치 두 개를 가로·세로로 놓고, 모든 자리의 오차를 색으로 칠한 지도: A map with two weights placed across and up-down, every spot colored by its error. The darker, the smaller the error. Learning means finding and descending to low places on this landscape.
흰 공이 지금 가중치예요. 금색 원이 가장 낮은 바닥이에요. 공이 금색: The white ball is the current weights. The gold circle is the lowest bottom. It succeeds when the ball gets inside the gold circle and nearly stops.
한 걸음의 크기예요. 너무 작으면 바닥까지 오래 걸리고, 너무 크면 골짜: The size of one step. Too small and it takes ages to reach the bottom; too big and it flies off across the valley.
\"한 걸음\"을 눌러 공을 한 번 굴려 보세요. 공은 지금 자리에서 가: Press "One step" to roll the ball once. The ball goes in the steepest downhill direction from where it is.
지형의 한 점 = 직선 하나: One point on the landscape = one straight line
공이 움직이면 뉴런이 긋는 직선도 바뀌어요. 바닥에 가까울수록 선이 노란: As the ball moves, the line the neuron draws changes too. The closer to the bottom, the better the line passes through the four yellow points.
학습률을 골라 \"멈출 때까지\"를 누르고, 공이 바닥에 멈추면 채점하세: Pick a learning rate and press "Until it stops," and check when the ball stops at the bottom (Space).
생명체가 칸을 한 칸씩 움직이는 세상이에요. 노란 칸에 들어가면 보상을: A world where the creature moves one cell at a time. Stepping into a yellow cell gives a reward and ends the episode. This time each cell gets written with "the points I'll get from here on," that is, its value.
칸의 숫자가 가치, 화살표가 가장 좋은 방향이에요. 처음에는 아무것도 몰: The number in a cell is its value, and the arrow is the best direction. At first it knows nothing, so they're all empty.
\"한 번 퍼뜨리기\"를 눌러 보세요. 목표 바로 옆 칸부터 가치가 생겨: Press "Spread once." Value appears starting from the cell right next to the goal.
한 칸씩 번지는 가치: Value spreading one cell at a time
누를 때마다 가치가 한 칸씩 더 멀리 번져요. 멀어질수록 할인율 γ만큼: Each press spreads value one cell further. The further away, the smaller it gets, by the discount γ. When it reaches the start (S), the gold path connects.
When the gold path reaches the goal, check (Space).
이번에는 점의 색이 셋이에요. 출력 뉴런도 셋이고, 각 출력은 \"그 색: This time the points come in three colors. There are three output neurons too, and each output is "the probability of that color."
세 출력은 소프트맥스로 묶여 있어서 합이 언제나 1이에요. 가장 큰 출력: The three outputs are tied together with softmax, so they always add up to 1. The color of the biggest output is the brain's answer.
배경은 그 자리에서 가장 큰 출력의 색이에요. 진할수록 확신이 커요. 경: The background is the color of the biggest output at that spot. The darker, the more confident. On the boundary the two colors' probabilities are equal.
Drag the x coordinate to output 3 to connect it. The right side turns green.
맞은 점 수와 정답 색의 확률 평균이 나와요. 모든 점이 맞으면 채점하세: This shows the number of correct points and the average probability of the correct color. When every point is right, check (Space).
이번 장의 입력은 두 갈래예요. 하나는 값, 하나는 문(0 = 닫힘, 1: In this chapter the input comes in two lines. One is a value, the other a gate (0 = closed, 1 = open). The output must match the value exactly.
값과 문이 칸마다 함께 들어와요. 목표 줄은 문이 열린 칸에서만 값이 나: The value and the gate come in together in each cell. The target row shows the value only in cells where the gate is open, and 0 where it's closed.
출력 뉴런을 눌러 아래에서 활성화 함수를 \"곱(×)\"으로 바꿔 보세요: Click the output neuron and change its activation function below to "Multiply (×)." A multiply neuron multiplies all incoming signals.
이제 값 A와 문 B를 둘 다 출력에 이으면, 문이 0일 때 곱이 0이: Now connect both value A and gate B to the output: when the gate is 0 the product is 0, so the value is blocked. When every cell is right, check (Space).
학습 실험에서는 가중치를 직접 고치지 않아요. 뉴런이 이 진리표를 보면서: In training experiments you don't fix the weights yourself. The neuron fixes them on its own while looking at this truth table.
한 번 배울 때 가중치를 얼마나 크게 고칠지 정해요. 너무 작으면 느리고: Sets how much to change the weights in one round of learning. Too small is slow; too big and it can't learn.
네 줄을 한 번씩 보고, 줄마다 틀린 만큼 가중치를 고쳐요. 이것을 학습: It looks at the four rows once each and fixes the weights by how wrong each row was. This is called one round of learning (an epoch).
맞힐 때까지 계속 배워요(Space). 다시 누르면 멈춰요. 처음 가중치: Keeps learning until it gets them right (Space). Press again to stop. Reset weights (R) erases what it learned and starts over.
The lower the red line goes, the better it's learning.
선 위 숫자가 학습할 때마다 스스로 바뀌어요. 선이나 뉴런을 클릭하면 지: The numbers on the lines change by themselves with every round of learning. Click a line or neuron to see its current value.

뉴런은 신호를 받아서 다음으로 넘겨 주는 작은 계산기예요. 이 게임에서는: A neuron is a small calculator that takes in signals and passes one on. In this game each circle is a neuron, and the lines joining circles are synapses. Signals flow along a line in one direction only. The more neurons you join, the more complex the things they can do.
가중치는 선 하나의 \"세기\"예요. 같은 신호라도 세기가 2인 선을 지: A weight is the "strength" of one line. The same signal is doubled through a line of strength 2 and halved through one of 0.5. At 0 nothing gets through, and a negative strength pushes toward off instead. When we say AI "learns", we mean it adjusts these strengths to good values.
한 뉴런에 선이 여러 개 들어오면, 각 선으로 온 값을 모두 더해요. 예: When several lines come into one neuron, it adds up the values from every line. For example, if A is 1 with strength 1 and B is 1 with strength 1, the sum is 2. In this game a sum of 0.5 or more counts as on (1).
문턱은 \"얼마나 모여야 켜질까\"를 정하는 기준이에요. 언제나 1을 보: The threshold is the bar for "how much must gather before it turns on". Joining the always-on neuron (always 1) with a negative line always takes a fixed amount off the sum, so more signal must gather to turn on. This value is called the bias. Changing the bias makes the same input easier or harder to turn on.
음수 가중치는 빨간 선이에요. 보내는 뉴런이 켜질수록 받는 뉴런의 합을: A negative weight is a red line. The more the sending neuron is on, the more it cuts the receiving neuron's sum. Use it to say "if this is on, turn off". Real brains have a great many of these inhibiting signals too.
XOR은 \"둘이 다를 때만 켜짐\"이에요. 뉴런 하나는 평면에 직선 하: XOR means "on only when the two differ". One neuron can only draw a single straight line on a plane, so it can't make this. So you put hidden neurons in the middle, give each a small condition ("only A on", "only B on"), and add them at the output. Stacking layers like this is a multilayer perceptron.
"All three the same" means "all three on" or "all three off". To give each case to one hidden neuron, you must work out the threshold exactly. It is practice at finding a value that is passed only when all three are on, and not when just two are.
\"A 그리고 B가 아님\"은 켜는 선(A, +)과 끄는 선(B, -)을: "A and not B" is made by joining an on-line (A, +) and an off-line (B, -) to the same neuron. It is a way to add one exception to a condition.
"Only when equal" means "both on" or "both off". Split the hard condition into two easy ones, then combine them at the end with "or" (OR).
다수결은 \"켜진 개수가 몇 개 이상인가\"예요. 모든 입력을 같은 세기: Majority means "are at least so many on?". If every input is added with the same strength, the sum is simply the number that are on, so you only need the right threshold.
\"딱 하나만\"은 한 번에 풀기 어려워요. \"하나 이상 켜짐\"과 \: "Exactly one" is hard to solve in one go. Build "one or more on" and "two or more on" separately, then take the second away from the first, and only "exactly one" is left. It is practice at splitting a big problem into small ones.
반가산기는 한 자리 덧셈 기계예요. 1 + 1 = 2를 이진수로 쓰면 1: A half adder is a one-digit adding machine. 1 + 1 = 2 is written 10 in binary, so this digit (the sum) is 0 and the digit carried to the next place (the carry) is 1. The sum can be made with XOR and the carry with AND. Computers add by chaining circuits like this.
NAND는 \"둘 다 켜졌을 때만 꺼짐\"이에요. NAND만 여러 개 이: NAND means "off only when both are on". You can build any logic circuit from NANDs alone, so it is used as a basic part of computer chips.
이진수에서는 자리마다 값이 달라요. 2의 자리는 1의 자리보다 두 배 중: In binary, each digit is worth a different amount. The 2s digit matters twice as much as the 1s digit. So if you give the lines strengths that double with the digit's value, one neuron can compare two numbers.
편향은 \"아무 감각이 없어도 기본으로 내보내는 값\"이에요. 생명체에게: The bias is "the value sent out by default, even with no senses at all". The creature has an always-on neuron that always sends 1, so joining it to the wheels makes it go forward even when it sees nothing.
바퀴 두 개의 빠르기가 다르면 느린 쪽으로 휘어요. 왼쪽 눈을 오른바퀴에: If the two wheels turn at different speeds, the creature curves toward the slower side. If you join the left eye to the right wheel crosswise, then when food is on the left the right wheel speeds up and the body turns toward the food. This is a crossed connection.
반사는 생각하지 않고 바로 하는 반응이에요. 뜨거운 걸 만지면 손을 바로: A reflex is a reaction that happens at once, without thinking. Just as you pull your hand back from something hot, join one line so the creature dodges the other way as soon as a feeler senses a thorn.
억제는 신호를 깎는 빨간 선이에요. 눈이 밝을수록 바퀴를 느리게 하면,: Inhibition is a red line that cuts a signal. If the wheels slow down as the eyes get brighter, the creature goes slower and slower as it nears the light, then stops.
수염은 벽에 닿으면 그쪽이 켜지는 감각이에요. 닿은 쪽 바퀴를 빠르게 하: Whiskers are a sense that turns on on the side that touches a wall. If the wheel on the touched side speeds up, the body turns away from the wall and goes around it.
히든 뉴런은 감각과 바퀴 사이에 있는 \"중간 생각\"이에요. \"빛이: A hidden neuron is a "middle thought" between the senses and the wheels. A judgment that combines conditions, like "even if you see light, don't chase it if you feel thorns", needs a middle step.
적대적 예제는 AI를 일부러 속이려고 만든 입력이에요. 아귀의 미끼는 먹: An adversarial example is an input made on purpose to fool an AI. The anglerfish's lure glows like food and fools a simple brain. Not to be fooled, it must look not only at the light but also at other signals (thorns).
학습은 틀린 만큼 가중치를 조금씩 고치는 일이에요. 정답과 출력의 차이(: Learning means fixing the weights a little at a time, by as much as they were wrong. It measures the gap between the answer and the output (the error) and changes the line strengths in the direction that shrinks the error, over and over. No one has to fix them one by one.
학습률은 한 번에 얼마나 크게 고칠지예요. 너무 작으면 아주 오래 걸리고: The learning rate is how big a fix to make at once. Too small and it takes a very long time; too big and it shoots past the answer and never learns. Choosing a good value matters.
뉴런 하나는 평면에 직선 하나만 그을 수 있어요. XOR처럼 직선 하나로: One neuron can only draw a single straight line on a plane. A problem like XOR, which no single straight line can split, can't be solved no matter how long it learns. That is why hidden neurons are needed.
역전파는 출력에서 생긴 오차를 거꾸로 히든 뉴런에게도 나눠 주는 방법이에: Backpropagation passes the error from the output back to the hidden neurons too. Telling each one "the output was this wrong, so you are this much to blame" lets every line be fixed together. Nearly every AI today learns this way.
강화학습은 정답을 알려 주지 않고 점수만 주는 학습이에요. 생명체는 여러: Reinforcement learning gives only scores, never the right answer. The creature tries many times and slowly changes toward what earned more points. Deciding what to give points for is the human's job.
먹었을 때만 점수를 주면, 우연히 먹기 전까지는 무엇이 좋은지 알 수 없: If you give points only for eating, it can't tell what is good until it eats by chance. Giving small points for getting closer to food too makes the way easier to find. It splits a big goal into small rewards.
점수는 깎을 수도 있어요. 하지 않았으면 하는 일(가시에 찔리기)에 벌점: Points can be taken away too. Give a penalty for what you don't want (being pricked by thorns), and it learns to avoid that.

가중치는 경계선의 기울기를, 편향은 경계선의 위치를 정해요. x 쪽 가중: The weights set the boundary's slope, and the bias sets its position. A bigger weight on x stands the line upright, and changing the bias slides the line sideways, parallel to itself.
히든 뉴런 하나는 선 하나를 맡아요. 선 두 개를 합치면 띠를, 네 개를: One hidden neuron handles one line. Combine two lines and you get a band; combine four and you get a box-like shape. The more lines you gather, the more complex the shapes you can make.
히든 뉴런을 충분히 많이 쓰면 어떤 모양의 경계든 원하는 만큼 비슷하게: With enough hidden neurons, you can match a boundary of any shape as closely as you like. This is called universal approximation. It is why neural networks can do so many kinds of jobs.
과적합은 문제를 이해하지 않고 답만 외운 상태예요. 훈련 데이터는 다 맞: Overfitting is memorizing the answers without understanding the problem. It gets all the training data right but fails on data it hasn't seen. That is why an AI's skill is measured with test data not used in training. Forcing a fit to mislabeled points makes the boundary wiggly.
Gradient descent moves the weights a little at a time in the direction that lowers the error. It is like walking down a mountain with your eyes closed, one step at a time, toward where the ground slopes down. Repeat it, and the boundary finds the right place by itself.
층을 쌓으면 앞 층이 만든 결과를 뒤 층이 다시 조합할 수 있어요. 선: Stacking layers lets a later layer recombine what an earlier layer made. Mix the judgments from two lines once more, and even a complex shape like a checkerboard can be split. The "deep" in "deep learning" means layers stacked deep like this.
필터는 3×3 크기의 작은 돋보기예요. 그림 위를 한 칸씩 옮겨 다니며,: A filter is a small 3×3 magnifying glass. It slides over the picture one cell at a time, adding up (picture × filter) over the cells it covers. The more a spot looks like the filter, the bigger the value. Since the same filter is used everywhere in the picture, it finds the pattern wherever it is.
특징 맵은 필터 하나가 그림 전체를 훑고 남긴 결과 지도예요. 필터가 찾: A feature map is the result map a filter leaves after sweeping over the whole picture. Only the spots with the pattern the filter looks for light up. Change the filter, and the same picture gives a completely different map.
경계는 밝기가 갑자기 바뀌는 곳이에요. 필터 한쪽은 -, 다른 쪽은 +로: An edge is where brightness suddenly changes. Paint one side of the filter - and the other side +, and the value grows only at spots that are "dark on the left and bright on the right". Human eyes look for edges like this first, too.
풀링은 특징 맵에서 가장 큰 값 하나만 뽑아 요약하는 일이에요. \"이: Pooling sums up a feature map by picking only its largest value. It keeps just "is this pattern somewhere in the picture?". The flow filter → feature map → pooling → output is the whole of a CNN.
두 특징이 함께 있는 자리는 각 특징만 있는 자리보다 필터와 겹치는 칸이: A spot where two features meet overlaps more cells of the filter than a spot with only one feature. Split that difference with a threshold (bias), and you can find just "where the two meet".
지금까지의 뇌는 지금 들어온 입력만 보고 답했어요. 순환 신경망(RNN): Until now the brain answered by looking only at the current input. A recurrent neural network (RNN) feeds the value it just gave back to itself, so it can remember what came before. It is used for data with an order, like text or sound.
출력이 자기 자신에게 되돌아오면, 한 번 켜진 값을 계속 붙잡아 둘 수: When the output comes back to itself, it can hold on to a value once it turns on. It is like a switch that stays on after you let go.
같은 입력이라도 앞에 무엇이 왔느냐에 따라 뜻이 달라져요. \"지금\"과: The same input can mean different things depending on what came before it. Looking at "now" and "just before (memory)" together lets it notice order patterns like "twice in a row".
기억은 바로 한 칸 전 것만 돌아와요. 더 오래된 일을 기억하려면 기억을: Memory only brings back what was one cell before. To remember older things, memory must be passed down the line to the next neuron. The longer it is passed along, the fainter the signal tends to get, so long memory is something RNNs find hard.
숫자를 끝없이 셀 필요 없이, 필요한 것 하나만 \"상태\"로 기억하면: There's no need to count forever; just remember the one thing you need as a "state". For odd/even, remember only "has it been odd so far?", and flip it when a new 1 comes.
변화를 알아채려면 지금과 바로 전을 둘 다 알아야 해요. 둘이 다른지는: To notice a change, you must know both now and just before. Whether the two differ is decided with XOR. This problem uses memory and logic together.
비지도 학습은 정답(색) 없이 데이터 속에서 비슷한 것끼리 묶는 학습이에: Unsupervised learning groups similar things in the data without any answers (colors). Even with no one naming the groups, it finds them from the way the points gather.
k-평균은 두 단계를 되풀이해요. ① 묶기: 점마다 가장 가까운 중심의: k-means repeats two steps. ① Group: each point takes the color of its nearest center. ② Move: each center goes to the middle of the points of its color. It ends when the centers stop moving.
지역 최소는 \"여기가 가장 낮은 곳인 줄 알고 멈췄는데, 사실 더 낮은: A local minimum is when it stops, thinking "this is the lowest place", but a lower place actually exists elsewhere. With a bad start, k-means gets stuck in a wrong answer like this. Choosing a good start matters.
무리 수 k를 늘리면 점과 중심 사이 거리 합은 늘 줄어들어요. 하지만: As the number of groups k grows, the total distance between points and centers always shrinks. But from some point on, it hardly shrinks at all. That bend (the elbow) is the right number of groups.
오토인코더는 입력을 작은 코드로 줄였다가(인코더) 다시 원래대로 살려 내: An autoencoder is a brain that shrinks the input into a small code (encoder) and then brings it back as it was (decoder). To bring it back, the code must hold only the information that really matters, so it learns to pull out the core of the data.
코드가 놓이는 공간을 잠재 공간이라고 해요. 코드 두 칸이면 평면 위의: The space where codes sit is called the latent space. A two-slot code is one point on a plane. Each input must sit in a different spot to be brought back.
작은 코드에는 \"어느 무늬인가\" 같은 중요한 정보만 들어가고, 한 칸: A small code only holds the important information, like "which pattern is it", and noise that flips one cell at a time can't get through. So drawing again from the code gives a clean pattern.
표현 학습은 쓸모 있는 코드를 사람이 정해 주지 않고 AI가 스스로 찾게: Representation learning lets the AI find a useful code by itself, instead of a person deciding it. Even with just "bring it back" as the goal, after learning each input ends up with its own code.
코드는 0과 1만 쓸 필요가 없어요. 0, 0.5, 1처럼 크기를 나눠: A code doesn't have to use only 0 and 1. Using sizes like 0, 0.5 and 1 lets one slot hold three or more things. The decoder reads that size back with thresholds.
오차 지형은 가중치마다 오차가 얼마인지 그린 지도예요. 낮은 곳일수록 오: An error landscape is a map of how big the error is for each set of weights. The lower the spot, the smaller the error. Learning is like rolling a ball on this landscape down to the lowest place.
모멘텀은 지난 걸음의 속도를 기억해서 같은 쪽으로 계속 가려는 힘(관성): Momentum remembers the speed of past steps and keeps pushing the same way (inertia). A ball that only bounced between the walls of a narrow valley rolls straight toward the bottom thanks to inertia.
경사 하강은 발밑만 보기 때문에 작은 웅덩이에 빠지면 거기가 바닥인 줄: Gradient descent only looks at the ground under its feet, so if it falls into a small dip it stops, thinking it is the bottom. Get over the dip's edge with inertia, or change the starting point, and it can find a deeper bottom.
Adam은 가중치마다 걸음 크기를 따로 맞춰요. 가파른 쪽은 작게, 평평: Adam sizes the step separately for each weight. It takes small steps where it is steep and big steps where it is flat, so it goes down well in any direction. It is the most widely used method in neural network training today.
가치는 \"이 칸에 있으면 앞으로 점수를 얼마나 받을까\"예요. 목표 가: Value is "how many points can I expect from here on if I'm in this cell". Cells closer to the goal have more value. With value written in every cell, just going toward bigger value reaches the goal.
할인율 γ는 \"나중에 받을 점수를 지금 얼마로 칠까\"예요. γ가 작으: The discount γ is "how much is a later reward worth right now". A small γ prefers a small reward right in front; a big γ prefers a big reward far away.
Q러닝은 지도를 모르는 채로 직접 돌아다니며 배워요. 칸마다 네 방향의: Q-learning learns by walking around without knowing the map. Each cell keeps a score table (Q) for the four directions, and after every step it fixes the table a little based on the points it actually got.
늘 가장 좋다고 아는 쪽으로만 가면(활용) 더 좋은 곳을 영영 못 찾을: If you only ever go where you think is best (exploitation), you may never find a better place. Sometimes you need to go anywhere on purpose (exploration). ε is how often.
소프트맥스는 여러 출력이 합쳐서 1이 되도록 나눠 가지게 해요. 그래서: Softmax makes several outputs share so they add up to 1. So each output can be read as "the probability of that answer". Just pick the answer with the biggest probability.
맞힌 것과 확신하는 것은 달라요. 가중치를 크게 하면 출력 사이의 차이가: Getting it right and being sure are different. Bigger weights widen the gap between outputs, so the probability leans to one side (more confidence). On the other hand, being too sure means being badly wrong when it is wrong.
갈래가 많아도 방법은 같아요. 출력 뉴런마다 \"내 갈래일수록 커지게\": With many classes, the method is the same. Join each output neuron so it "grows the more it is its own class", and the biggest output is the answer.
교차 엔트로피는 \"정답의 확률이 얼마나 낮았나\"로 오차를 재요. 정답: Cross-entropy measures the error by "how low the right answer's probability was". If it is sure of the right answer the error is near 0, and the lower the right answer's probability, the bigger the error gets. Used with softmax, the amount to fix becomes simply "probability - answer".
게이트(문)는 값에 0이나 1을 곱해서 통과시키거나 막는 장치예요. 곱(: A gate multiplies a value by 0 or 1 to let it through or block it. Join a gate signal to a multiply (×) neuron, and the value passes unchanged only when the gate is open (1).
The input gate decides "should the value coming in now be stored in memory?". It stores a new value only when the store signal comes, and otherwise leaves the old memory alone.
망각 게이트는 \"지난 기억을 남길까 지울까\"를 정하는 문이에요. 지울: The forget gate decides "keep the old memory or erase it?". When it is time to erase, it multiplies the stored memory by 0 and starts over.
LSTM은 입력 · 망각 · 출력 문 세 개를 단 기억 칸이에요. 필요할: An LSTM is a memory cell with three gates: input · forget · output. It stores only when needed, erases when needed, and lets out only when needed. That is why it remembers long sequences well.
데이터의 대부분이 한쪽이면, 모두 그쪽이라고만 답해도 정확도가 높게 나와: If most of the data is on one side, just answering that side every time gives high accuracy. But it may not find a single one of the rare side (patients). That is why you must also check "how many of the ones to find did it find" (recall).
AI는 정답과 함께 자주 나오는 쉬운 단서(지름길)를 배우기 쉬워요. 늑: AI easily learns an easy clue that often shows up with the answer (a shortcut). If every wolf photo is in snow, it learns "snow = wolf". You have to check that the data isn't lopsided.
입력을 살짝만 바꿔도 답이 뒤집히는 AI는 쉽게 속아요. 경계를 두 무리: An AI whose answer flips when the input changes just a little is easily fooled. Put the boundary right in the middle of the two groups to leave room on both sides, and it can hold even for slightly pushed inputs.
히든 뉴런들이 똑같은 가중치로 출발하면, 똑같이 계산하고 똑같이 고쳐져서: If hidden neurons start with exactly the same weights, they compute the same and get fixed the same, staying twins forever. Then it is the same as having one neuron. That is why the starting weights are set a little differently (at random).
커넥톰은 뇌 속 모든 뉴런이 어떻게 이어져 있는지 그린 지도예요. 대결에: A connectome is a map of how every neuron in a brain is connected. Like the brains that competed in battles, the same senses can behave completely differently depending on how they are wired.
